steps.message: Garrett wants the Phase 3 estimate out to the surety broker and I don't want it going anywhere until Section 2 has been checked against what's actually on the plans. The estimate is DSR_Ph3_Engineers_Estimate in Cost Estimates; the drainage sheets are C-6, C-8 and C-9 in DSR_Ph3_Improvement_Plans_C1-C9 under Design-Drafting, and the pipe reaches are scheduled in DSR_Ph3_StormDrain_HGL in Reports-Studies. Give me the corrected Section 2 subtotal, a line-by-line table of every quantity or unit-price change with the sheet it comes off, and the revised rounded bond figure. Stay in Section 2, but if something shown on the plans is missing from the estimate, it belongs in the reconciliation. Price off the published schedule — where it gives an "Actual" the amount already carried stands. Flag an item only where the schedule has nothing matching what the plans show, and leave the amount already carried in the subtotal for anything you flag. Where the plans give no dimension or stationing for a line item already in the estimate, the quantity already carried stands. Round pipe lengths to the next whole foot. Put it in a memo to Callaway for my signature, dated 10/31/2026, saved as Correspondence/Client/Memo_to_Callaway_2026-10-31.docx.

PREFACE
The Uniform Unit Cost Schedule is published by Clark County Public Works for use by engineers of record, developers,
and sureties in preparing an engineer's estimate of probable cost for subdivision improvements offered for bonding under
Clark County Code Title 30 and the Uniform Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction Off-Site
Improvements (Clark County Area).
Unit prices set forth in this schedule reflect current Southern Nevada construction market conditions as surveyed by the
Department across the twelve-month period preceding the effective date, drawing on bid tabulations for publicly bid
subdivision and off-site improvement work in unincorporated Clark County and the incorporated municipalities of the Las
Vegas Valley. The schedule is intended to normalize bonding across projects and to remove unit price disputes from the
plan check cycle.
Engineer's estimates for subdivision performance and labor-and-material bonds submitted to Clark County shall use the
unit prices published in this schedule unless project-specific pricing is documented in writing (three qualified
subcontractor quotes or an executed prime contract, dated within ninety (90) days of estimate submittal) and approved by
Clark County Development Review prior to bond posting. Where project-specific pricing is approved, the higher of the
two unit prices shall govern for bonding purposes.
Contingency, mobilization, and design/inspection allowances stated in Section 11 shall be applied to the sum of itemized
construction cost in every engineer's estimate submitted for bonding.
ESCALATION AND REVIEW
This schedule is reviewed annually by the Department. Revised schedules are issued each January, with an effective date
of 01/01 of the calendar year. Between annual issues, the Department may issue a mid-year addendum where documented
market conditions materially depart (±10 percent or greater on any category) from the published unit price. Bonding
accepted against a superseded schedule remains in force at the amount posted; renewals, reissues, and increases occurring
after a schedule effective date shall use the current schedule.
Estimates submitted within thirty (30) days after a schedule effective date may, at the applicant's election, be computed
against the immediately superseded schedule.

WHEREAS, the County requires, as a condition of approval of the final map for Phase 2 and of the

WHEREAS, concurrently herewith the Subdivider has caused a performance and guaranty bond to be

NOW, THEREFORE, for and in consideration of the mutual promises herein contained, the approval of
the Phase 2 final map, and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are
acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:
ARTICLE I. CONSTRUCTION OF THE WORK
1.1   The Subdivider, at its sole cost and expense, and at no cost or expense to the County, shall construct and
complete all of the Work, consisting of both the offsite improvements and the onsite improvements set forth in
the Plans and itemized in Exhibit A, including but not limited to collector road half-improvements, offsite signal
modifications, offsite storm drain trunk connection, internal streets, storm drain, wet and dry utilities, and
monumentation.
1.2   The Work shall be constructed in accordance with the Clark County Code, the Uniform Standard
Specifications for Public Works’ Construction Off-Site Improvements — Clark County Area, the Plans as
approved by the Director of Public Works, any and all permits issued by the County, and other requirements of
the County.
1.3   The Subdivider shall obtain, prior to commencement of any portion of the Work, all required permits,
including but not limited to an offsite improvement permit, onsite construction permits, and permits required by
other local, County, State and Federal agencies.
ARTICLE II. APPROVAL OF PLANS; PRECONDITIONS TO CONSTRUCTION
2.1   No portion of the Work shall commence until:
(a)   The Plans have been approved by the Director of Public Works (“Director”);
(b)   All plan-check and inspection fees required by Title 30 of the Clark County Code have been paid;
(c)   The security required by Article IV has been executed and delivered to the County; and
(d)   All applicable permits have been issued.
ARTICLE III. NOTICE OF COMMENCEMENT AND INSPECTIONS
3.1   The Subdivider shall notify the Director at least twenty-four (24) hours in advance of commencement of
any of the items of Work enumerated in Chapter 30.32 of the Clark County Code, including without limitation
the placing of sewer, water, gas, power, telephone lines and fire hydrants; the backfilling of the same; the
placing of concrete for curb, gutter, sidewalk, valley gutters, storm drain structures, manholes and
street-lighting foundations; the placing of Type I and Type II gravel base course; the priming of base course; the
placing of street lighting; and the placing of street name signs and traffic-control signs.
3.2   The Subdivider shall comply with Chapter 30.32 of the Clark County Code in obtaining inspections of the
Work from the County.

ARTICLE IV. SECURITY
4.1   As security for the faithful performance of this Agreement and the completion of the Work, the Subdivider
shall deliver to the County the Bond in the penal sum of $3,200,000, being the aggregate of the offsite subtotal
and the onsite subtotal set forth in Exhibit A.
4.2   The security is furnished pursuant to Title 30 of the Clark County Code and is a condition precedent to
approval of the Phase 2 final map and issuance of the offsite improvement permit and onsite construction
permits.
4.3   The security shall remain in full force and effect until the Work has been accepted by the County pursuant
to Article VI and released pursuant to Article VII, and any warranty period applicable to the accepted Work has
expired.
ARTICLE V. ADJUSTMENT OF UTILITIES; COMPLIANCE
5.1   The Subdivider shall, at its sole cost and expense, make all adjustments to existing utilities necessitated by
the Work.
5.2   The Subdivider shall perform and complete the Work in accordance with the Clark County Code, all
applicable permits, the Plans, and other requirements of the County. The County retains the right to require
corrections at any time before release of the security pursuant to Article VII, even where the Plans have been
previously approved by the Director.
ARTICLE VI. INSPECTION AND ACCEPTANCE
6.1   The Work shall be inspected by the County in accordance with Chapter 30.32 of the Clark County Code.
Ordinarily, no less than one continuous block of any single item of Work will be inspected and approved.
6.2   The offsite improvements and the onsite improvements shall be inspected and processed for acceptance as
separate components. Each component shall be subject to a prefinal and final inspection by the County. Upon
satisfactory completion of the applicable inspections and receipt of any punchlist corrections, the Director of
Public Works, or his designee, may issue a written acceptance of the component. Written acceptance of a
component may occur at different times for the offsite component and the onsite component.
6.3   Inspection or approval of any item of Work, or a portion of the Work, shall not forfeit the right of the
County to require corrections to quality, workmanship or materials at any time prior to written acceptance of the
applicable component, notwithstanding any prior approval issued by oversight.
ARTICLE VII. RELEASE OF SECURITY
7.1   The provisions of this Article VII shall govern the release of the security posted under Article IV and the
Bond attached hereto.
7.2   Release provision. The Subdivider may request in writing partial or full release of the bonded amount
corresponding to any component of the Work upon written acceptance of that component of the Work by Clark
County Public Works. Offsite and onsite improvements shall be treated as separate components and may be
accepted, and their corresponding bond amounts released, independently, upon prefinal and final inspection.
7.3   The bonded amount corresponding to each component of the Work is the subtotal for that component as set
forth in Exhibit A. The offsite component is bonded in the amount of $1,100,000 and the onsite component is
bonded in the amount of $2,100,000, together totaling the penal sum of the Bond.
7.4   A written request for release of security shall reference this Agreement, the Bond number, the recording
instrument number of this Agreement, and the component or components for which release is sought, and shall
attach the County’s written acceptance of the applicable component. The County will process the release in the
ordinary course upon confirmation that the applicable component has been accepted pursuant to Article VI and

accordance with Title 30 of the Clark County Code prior to release of performance security for the applicable
component.
ARTICLE VIII. DEFAULT; REMEDIES
8.1   In the event the Subdivider fails to commence or complete the Work, or any portion of the Work, within
the period allowed by the applicable permit, or is otherwise in default of this Agreement, the County may call
upon the Bond for completion of the Work in accordance with the Plans.
8.2   In the event of a threat or danger to the health, safety or welfare of the public arising from the Subdivider’s
work, as solely determined by the Director, the Subdivider shall, at its sole cost, immediately eliminate the
threat as directed by the County. Upon failure to do so, the County may proceed against the Bond or complete
the Work itself and invoice the Subdivider.
ARTICLE IX. INDEMNITY AND INSURANCE
9.1   The Subdivider shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless the County, its officers, employees and agents
from and against any and all claims, damages, losses and expenses (including reasonable attorneys’ fees) arising
out of or resulting from the Subdivider’s performance of the Work.
9.2   The Subdivider shall maintain commercial general liability insurance with combined single limits of not
less than $2,000,000 per occurrence, and shall name the County as an additional insured, in accordance with the
County’s standard insurance requirements for offsite improvement agreements.
ARTICLE X. GENERAL PROVISIONS
10.1   Recording. This Agreement shall be recorded in the Official Records of the Clark County Recorder and
shall run with the land comprising Phase 2 of the Subdivision.
10.2   Successors. This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the Parties and their
respective successors and assigns.
10.3   Governing law. This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the
State of Nevada, and venue for any action arising hereunder shall lie in Clark County, Nevada.
10.4   Entire agreement. This Agreement, together with Exhibit A and the Bond attached hereto, constitutes
the entire agreement between the Parties with respect to the Phase 2 Work and supersedes all prior negotiations
and understandings.

Dear Mr. Braddock:
Development Review has completed the first-round plan check of the Desert Sage Ranch Phase 3 improvement
plan set (Sheets C-1 through C-9), the associated final map, and the supporting studies transmitted with the
08/21/2026 submittal. The plans have been circulated to Grading and Drainage, Landscape, Fire Access (via
the Clark County Fire Department), Utilities (via the appropriate purveyors), and Mapping (via the County
Surveyor).
Comments are organized in two parts:
• General Comments are binding and must be resolved before Public Works can recommend approval.
Please respond to each item in the Response column and return the annotated matrix with the resubmittal
package. Where a comment calls for a plan revision, mark the corresponding sheet with a revision triangle
and update the revision block.
• Advisory Comments are informational only and do not require a written response. They are provided so
that the design team is aware of items the reviewer noted that may affect future submittals, construction
inspection, or acceptance.
The next submittal should include (i) the annotated comment matrix, (ii) a red-lined set showing every change,
(iii) a clean set of revised sheets, and (iv) any revised or reissued supporting documents referenced below.
Please cite this letter by its application numbers on the transmittal.
If any comment is unclear or the design team believes an alternative approach is warranted, please contact the
undersigned before resubmittal to discuss.
GENERAL COMMENTS
Response to each item is required. Items must be resolved before plan approval.
Grading and Drainage

exit_code=0
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""AHPELE requirement scanner (stdlib only; runs inside the task container).

Finds requirement-like statements in the text corpus written by
ahpele_index.py (/tmp/ahpele/corpus) so that hard constraints are not missed:

  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py            # scan: writes /tmp/ahpele/req_candidates.md and .csv
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --check    # coverage: lists candidates not yet reviewed
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --register FILE.csv|.xlsx   # register rows: is each value in the document it cites?

A candidate counts as reviewed when its ID (e.g. R0042) appears in
/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv (adopted) or /tmp/ahpele/rejected.csv (rejected,
with a reason). A whole document can be rejected by putting its path in
rejected.csv. The scanner is a recall aid: it misses requirements that live in
tables, drawings or images, and it lists many statements that are not hard
requirements. It knows nothing about any particular task.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import html
import json
import os
import re
import sys

OUT = "/tmp/ahpele"
STRONG = re.compile(
    r"\b(shall|must|is required|are required|required to|mandatory|not permitted|prohibited|shall not|"
    r"must not|may not exceed|no later than|condition of|subject to|is to|are to|(is|are)? ?limited to|"
    r"not (be )?(less|more|greater|lower|higher) than|not exceed|at least|at most|no more than|no less than|"
    r"maximum of|minimum of|is not allowed|are not allowed|will not be accepted|not acceptable)\b", re.I)
LIMIT = re.compile(
    r"(\b(not (to )?exceed|exceed(s|ing)?|maximum|minimum|max\.?|min\.?|at least|at most|no more than|"
    r"no less than|not less than|not more than|not greater than|up to|limit(ed|s)?|cap(ped)?|allowable|"
    r"permissible|permitted|threshold|tolerance|deadline|before|prior to|within|until|expires?|valid)\b|"
    r"[≤≥<>]=?|±|\+/-)", re.I)
NUMBER = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z])[-+]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?")
NOISE = re.compile(r"^(--- page \d+ ---|page \d+( of \d+)?|\W*)$", re.I)
MAX_LEN = 320
TAG = re.compile(r"<[^<>]{1,400}>")
# folders that usually hold general reference material (codes, standards, catalogues) rather than project documents
REFERENCE = re.compile(r"(^|/)(library|libraries|reference|references|standards?|codes?|regulations?|catalogues?|"
                       r"catalogs?|vendor|manufacturer)(/|$)", re.I)
# file names of published codes and standards (general engineering knowledge, not task-specific)
STANDARD_NAME = re.compile(
    r"^(\d+[ _-]?CFR|UFC|UFGS|UFM|ASCE|SEI|ACI|AISC|AISI|SDI|SJI|IBC|IRC|IFC[ _-]?\d|IECC|IEC|IEEE|NFPA|NEC|NESC|ISO|EN|"
    r"BS|ASTM|ASHRAE|ASME|AWS|AWWA|API|ANSI|UL|CSA|DIN|AS|NZS|TIA|FM|NEMA|OSHA|EPA|FEMA|AASHTO|MUTCD|ICC|NCHRP|"
    r"USACE|EM[ _-]\d|ETL|DoD|IS)[ _-]?\d", re.I)
DATA_TYPES = {"csv", "json"}
VOID_DIR = re.compile(r"(^|/)(archive[sd]?|superseded|obsolete|old|void|withdrawn|cancell?ed)(/|$)", re.I)


def load_inventory():
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(OUT, "inventory.json"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            return {r["path"]: r for r in json.load(fh).get("files", [])}
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}


def statements(text):
    """Yield (page, statement) pairs: lines joined into sentences, table rows kept whole."""
    page, buf = 1, []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"--- page (\d+) ---", raw.strip())
        if m:
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            page = int(m.group(1))
            continue
        line = raw.strip()
        if NOISE.match(line):
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            continue
        if "\t" in raw or " | " in line or line.count("  ") > 2:  # table-like row
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            yield page, re.sub(r"\s+", " ", line)
            continue
        buf.append(line)
        if re.search(r"[.;:]$", line) or len(" ".join(buf)) > 600:
            yield page, " ".join(buf)
            buf = []
    if buf:
        yield page, " ".join(buf)


def split_sentences(s):
    parts = re.split(r"(?<=[.;])\s+(?=[A-Z(])", s)
    return [p.strip() for p in parts if p.strip()]


def scan():
    corpus = os.path.join(OUT, "corpus")
    inv = load_inventory()
    rows = []
    data_like = {d for d, r in inv.items() if r.get("type") in DATA_TYPES}
    for dp, _, fns in os.walk(corpus):
        for fn in sorted(fns):
            if not fn.endswith(".txt"):
                continue
            full = os.path.join(dp, fn)
            doc = os.path.relpath(full, corpus)[:-4]
            try:
                text = open(full, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
            except OSError:
                continue
            if text.count("<") > 20 and len(TAG.findall(text[:20000])) > 20:  # XML / HTML: keep the text only
                text = html.unescape(TAG.sub(lambda m: "\n" if re.match(r"</?(p|div|tr|li|h\d|head|br|section|para)\b",
                                                                     m.group(0), re.I) else " ", text))
            seen = set()
            for page, st in statements(text):
                for s in split_sentences(st):
                    strong, limit, nums = bool(STRONG.search(s)), bool(LIMIT.search(s)), NUMBER.findall(s)
                    if not (strong or (limit and nums)) or (doc in data_like and not strong):
                        continue
                    key = s.lower()[:200]
                    if key in seen or len(s) < 12:
                        continue
                    seen.add(key)
                    score = (4 if nums else 3) if strong else 2  # 4: modal + number, 3: modal, 2: limit + number
                    rows.append({"doc": doc, "page": page, "score": score,
                                 "text": s if len(s) <= MAX_LEN else s[:MAX_LEN] + "…",
                                 "numbers": " ".join(nums[:8])})
    for r in rows:
        r["ref"] = bool(REFERENCE.search(os.path.dirname(r["doc"]))
                        or STANDARD_NAME.search(os.path.basename(r["doc"])))
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (r["ref"], r["doc"], r["page"]))
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, 1):
        r["id"] = f"R{i:04d}"
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv"), "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=["id", "doc", "page", "score", "ref", "numbers", "text"])
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)
    by_doc = {}
    for r in rows:
        by_doc.setdefault(r["doc"], []).append(r)
    lines = ["# Requirement candidates", "",
             f"{len(rows)} requirement-like statements in {len(by_doc)} documents (score 4: shall/must/"
             "not-more-than wording with a number; 3: the same wording without a number; 2: a limit word with a "
             "number, often context rather than a requirement). Tables, drawings and scanned pages are only partly covered: "
             "read those yourself. Status flags come from the FILE NAME; confirm which documents govern. Project "
             "documents come first; published codes and standards and documents in reference folders are listed "
             "last: the clauses that apply are the ones the project documents invoke. --check asks you to review the "
             "score 3-4 statements of project documents; use the rest when you look a requirement up.", ""]
    shown_ref = False
    for doc, rs in by_doc.items():
        if rs[0]["ref"] and not shown_ref:
            lines += ["# Reference folders (codes, standards, catalogues)", ""]
            shown_ref = True
        flags = inv.get(doc, {}).get("flags", "")
        lines.append(f"## {doc}" + (f"  [name flags: {flags}]" if flags else "") + f"  ({len(rs)})")
        for r in rs:
            lines.append(f"- {r['id']} p{r['page']} s{r['score']}: {r['text']}")
        lines.append("")
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]
    kdocs = {}
    for r in key:
        kdocs[r["doc"]] = kdocs.get(r["doc"], 0) + 1
    top = sorted(kdocs.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:10]
    print(f"requirement scan: {len(rows)} candidates in {len(by_doc)} documents -> {OUT}/req_candidates.md; "
          f"{len(key)} strong candidates in project documents to review"
          + (" (" + ", ".join(f"{d}: {n}" for d, n in top) + ")" if top else ""))
    return rows


def must_review(r):
    """Requirement wording (shall, must, is to, not more than ...) in project documents."""
    return int(r["score"]) >= 3 and str(r["ref"]) not in ("True", "1")


def read_text(path):
    try:
        return open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    except OSError:
        return ""


def check(limit):
    path = os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        scan()
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(fh))
    adopted = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "requirements.csv"))
    rejected = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "rejected.csv"))
    if not adopted.strip():
        print(f"{OUT}/requirements.csv is missing or empty: build the requirements table first "
              "(one row per hard requirement, with the candidate IDs it comes from).")
    ids = set(re.findall(r"\bR\d{4}\b", adopted + "\n" + rejected))
    rejected_docs = {r["doc"] for r in rows if r["doc"] in rejected}
    inv = load_inventory()
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]

    def covered(r):
        if r["id"] in ids:
            return True
        if r["doc"] not in rejected_docs:
            return False
        # rejecting a whole document covers its statements with a number only when the document is marked void
        # (status word in its file name, or an archive / superseded folder); otherwise each one needs its own ID
        return int(r["score"]) < 4 or bool(inv.get(r["doc"], {}).get("flags")) or bool(VOID_DIR.search(r["doc"]))

    open_rows = [r for r in key if not covered(r)]
    open_rows.sort(key=lambda r: (-int(r["score"]), r["doc"], int(r["page"])))
    n = len(key)
    print(f"coverage: {n - len(open_rows)}/{n} strong project-document candidates reviewed "
          f"({len(ids & {r['id'] for r in rows})} IDs cited in all, {len(rejected_docs)} documents rejected whole); "
          f"{len(open_rows)} not reviewed yet. ({len(rows) - n} weaker or code/standard candidates are optional: "
          f"see {OUT}/req_candidates.md.)")
    if not open_rows:
        print("Every candidate is adopted or rejected. Also check tables, drawings and scanned pages, which the "
              "scanner does not fully cover.")
        return 0
    print("Unreviewed candidates, strongest first (add each hard requirement to requirements.csv citing its ID, or "
          "list the ID with a reason in rejected.csv; a statement with a number in a document that is not marked "
          "void needs its own ID even if you rejected the document):")
    for r in open_rows[:limit]:
        print(f"- {r['id']} [{r['doc']} p{r['page']} s{r['score']}] {r['text'][:220]}")
    if len(open_rows) > limit:
        by = {}
        for r in open_rows[limit:]:
            by[r["doc"]] = by.get(r["doc"], 0) + 1
        print(f"... and {len(open_rows) - limit} more: " + ", ".join(f"{d} ({c})" for d, c in sorted(by.items())))
    return 1


SRC_COL = re.compile(r"source|clause|document|doc\b|ref|citation|basis|standard|section", re.I)
VAL_COL = re.compile(r"value|limit|threshold|criterion|criteria|requirement|min|max|allow", re.I)
CLAUSE_REF = re.compile(r"(§\s*[\w.()-]+|\b(?:clause|section|sec\.|para\.?|table|article|art\.)\s*[\w.()-]+)", re.I)


def norm_num(x):
    x = x.replace(",", "")

---
name: professional-memo
description: How to write an engineering memo, letter, reply, review response or technical note for a named recipient, written for an expert reader - answer first, basis from the record, every issue with owner and timing, exact scope, signature block, and a correct DOCX file. Use whenever the deliverable is a memo, letter, reply, response, review, disposition or note.
---

# Professional engineering memo

## Before writing
- Identify: who asked, who will act on the memo, the decision they must take, the "as of" date of the record, and any
  dates in the request (target date, deadline). Note what the request says is OUT of scope and leave it out.
- Gather the record: correspondence (emails, letters, RFIs), applications, studies, test reports, standards, contracts,
  tracking data in project applications. Build a dated timeline of relevant events in `/tmp/ahpele/timeline.md`.
- For each potential issue, find the exact source (document, section, date) and what it requires.
- For go/no-go questions (approve, issue, energise, accept, pay), do not stop at the first favourable reading. Build a checklist of every condition that applies
  (agreements, studies, permits, tests, payments, insurance, notices, deadlines, sign-offs, open correspondence) and
  check each one against the record as of the stated date. Only conclude that nothing blocks the decision after every
  condition has been checked and cited.

## Structure
1. Header: To / From / Date (use the record's "as of" date unless told otherwise) / Subject / project identifiers.
2. **Answer first**: one or two sentences that directly answer the question (yes / no / not yet, by which date), with
   the decisive reason.
3. **Basis**: the facts and requirements the answer rests on, each cited to the record (document, section, date).
4. **Open items** (one per issue): what it is; what requirement it rests on (cite it); what has to be done; who must do
   it (name the party or role, including the customer/applicant when it is theirs); whether it can be done before the
   target date and why; consequence if not.
5. Items reviewed and found acceptable, briefly, so the reader knows they were checked.
6. Scope statement: what this memo does not cover, exactly as the request defines it.
7. Recommendation / next steps with dates.
8. Signature block for the reviewing engineer if the request asks for one (name/title placeholders only where the
   request leaves the signer unnamed; never invent credentials).

## Determinations the reader can check
- Make a list of every question and request in the instruction (asks.md) and answer each one in its own labelled place.
- Each answer states the specific fact and the conclusion in one or two plain sentences: "<thing> is / is not <state>,
  because <fact with value and unit> (<document, section/sheet, date>)". Then give the working.
- When the record does not let you decide a question, say exactly what is missing, who must provide it and what the
  decision is meanwhile.
- Commit to one disposition per question, as engineering requests usually ask.
- Name the cause, not only the symptom: when something fails or is non-conforming, state why (which input, assumption,
  revision or condition) and what has to change.

## Scope, states and length
- Keep a scope ledger: what the request asks, what it excludes, what is under someone else's review. Items under separate
  review are mentioned, not decided; items that bear on the answer stay in even if raised elsewhere.
- Check the answer in every operating state or stage the request covers (before / during / after an event, normal and
  abnormal), not only the steady case.
- Length and precision follow the reader: a decision memo is usually 1-3 pages plus attachments; report numbers to the
  precision of the data (not six decimals); match tone and distribution to an internal or external recipient.

## Quality rules
- Be specific: dates, amounts, ratings, section numbers, document titles. No vague hedging.
- Distinguish facts from the record, requirements, and your engineering judgement.
- Check arithmetic and dates (business days, notice periods, expiry dates) with a script.
- Do not contradict yourself between the answer and the open items.
- Claim only actions that were actually taken (a request "has been sent" only if you sent it, with its record);
  otherwise write what should be done and by whom. Each follow-up becomes its own tracked item (ticket, task,
  register line with owner and date), not only a sentence inside a closed record.
- External letters carry no internal matters (internal case numbers, staff deliberations, other customers'
  correspondence, internal directives); keep those in the internal memo.
- Before netting a figure against a published baseline (capacity, budget, allowance), check what that baseline
  already includes and excludes, and say so.

## Producing the file
- Write DOCX with python-docx when available (`import docx`); otherwise use the word processing MCP tool if the task
  provides one, or build the file with LibreOffice (`soffice --headless --convert-to docx file.md` or `.html`).
- Use real headings and tables, not Markdown symbols inside the Word text.
- Save exactly at the path and file name the request gives; re-open the file to confirm it reads back, and run
  `python3 /tmp/ahpele/bin/ahpele_check.py <path>`.
- If the request also asks for actions in project applications (tickets, work packages, emails, calendar), do them
  too, and make their content consistent with the memo (see the workplace-apps skill).
- End with a final message that states the answer and lists every file and record you created.

name: cost-estimate-review
description: How a reviewer checks an engineer's estimate (bid/bond estimate) against plans and a published unit-price schedule - quantities by reach/station and structure count, unit consistency, exact price matching, rounding rules, extensions, subtotal, contingency and bond amount, plus a line-by-line reconciliation and scripted self-check. Use for any cost estimate, bond estimate, quantity or unit-price review.
---

# Engineer's estimate review

## 1. Set the rules before touching numbers
- Write down, from the instructions/estimate notes, every rule: which section(s) are in scope, the price source
  (schedule title, edition/date), what to do with items the schedule lacks, "Actual"/lump-sum handling, rounding
  (what, to what, up/nearest), the measurement convention, contingency %, bond % and bond rounding. These rules
  beat general practice. Quote them in the memo.
- Records: estimate (as carried: item no., description, unit, qty, unit price, extension), plan sheets (plan +
  profile + details + notes), schedules/worksheets (pipe schedule, structure table, HGL sheet), the price schedule.
  Use drawing-takeoff for counting and measuring from the sheets.

## 2. Quantities
- Linear items (pipe, curb, ditch) by reach: length = |station down - station up| for each reach between
  structures; sum per item (same size AND material/class). Cross-check plan stationing, profile, and any pipe
  schedule; when they disagree, report it and say which governs (profile/schedule usually carries the design
  length; plan callout may be rounded).
- Measurement convention matters: centre-to-centre of structures vs inside face to inside face (subtract half of
  each structure's inside dimension). Use the convention stated in the estimate, specification or schedule; if
  none, state the one used. Slope length = sqrt(dx^2 + dz^2) differs only for steep reaches.
- Don't forget laterals/connector pipes (inlet to main), stub-outs, outfall pipe beyond the last structure,
  and reaches drawn on another sheet across a match line.
- Count structures by type and size (inlet type, manhole diameter, junction box, headwall/endwall, flared end,
  cleanout, outlet structure, riprap pad). Each schedule/plan tag counts once; reconcile counts across sheets.
- Area/volume items: SY = SF/9, CY = CF/27; TON = CY x unit weight (use the stated density; riprap typically
  ~1.4-1.7 ton/CY in place - cite the source). Riprap pad volume = length x width x thickness.
- Items with no measurable basis on the plans: apply the instruction's rule for them, otherwise flag them; state
  which you did.
- Apply rounding only where instructed and only to the stated quantity (e.g. "round up" = ceiling, per item
  or per reach as the rule says - state which). Never round intermediate values otherwise.

## 3. Unit prices
- Match the schedule entry on description, size, material/class and unit exactly (24" RCP is not 24" HDPE; a
  48" manhole is not a 60" one; EA vs LF vs LS). Unit of the estimate must equal the schedule unit; convert the
  quantity, not the price, if they differ.
- Allowance / actual-cost / lump-sum items: follow the instruction's rule for them and state it.
- No matching schedule entry: flag it (what the plans show, the closest entries and why they do not fit); never
  invent or interpolate a price; treat the subtotal as the instruction directs.
- Watch for prices taken from the wrong size row, outdated schedule edition, or units swapped.

## 4. Arithmetic
- Extension = qty x unit price (to the cent). Subtotal = sum of extensions in the section. Then the estimate's own
  sequence: e.g. subtotal -> contingency (% of subtotal) -> total -> bond = stated % of the stated base (often
  100% performance; some agencies 110-125%, plus a labour-and-material bond of 50-100%). Follow the estimate's
  formula exactly and only change the inputs you corrected.
- Bond rounding: apply the stated rule (e.g. up to the next $1,000 or $100) once, at the end. Show the unrounded
  value, then the rounded one.
- Report other sections' totals unchanged if out of scope, but recompute the grand total and bond with the
  corrected section.

## 5. Reconciliation table (the deliverable core)
Columns: item no. | description | unit | qty carried | qty corrected | unit price carried | unit price corrected |
extension carried | extension corrected | delta | source (sheet + station/tag, schedule page/row) | note.
- One row for every change (quantity and/or price), plus rows for items shown on the plans but missing from the
  estimate (carried = 0) and items in the estimate with no plan basis (flag; keep or remove per the rules).
- Footer: carried subtotal, corrected subtotal, net delta (= sum of row deltas - check it), contingency, total,
  unrounded and rounded bond.

## 6. Self-check (do it with a script)
- Put every line in a CSV/JSON and recompute in Python with Decimal: per-reach lengths from stations, rounding per
  rule, extensions, subtotal, delta sum, contingency, bond and its rounding. Assert corrected subtotal - carried
  subtotal == sum(deltas).
- Re-read the estimate once more for lines you did not touch: confirm their arithmetic too (carried extension may
  itself be wrong - an arithmetic correction is a change and gets a row).
- Every number in the memo must match the script output and carry a unit ($, LF, EA, SY, CY, TON, LS) and a
  source. Give one corrected subtotal and one bond figure, not options.

At the south boundary of the built Phase 2 area, at the south terminus of Roadway A (Sta. 10+00, matching the
north subdivision line of the Phase 2 built area as shown on recorded final map NFM-24-0118), a
TEMPORARY CONSTRUCTION STUB — PHASE 3 CONNECTION has been constructed. The temporary
construction stub extends south from Sta. 10+00 into the currently undeveloped Phase 3 parcel and provides the
secondary point of access for Phase 2 while Phase 3 remains undeveloped.
As-built configuration.
• Extends approximately 180 feet north of the built Phase 2 curb line into the Phase 3 remainder parcel,
terminating at a graded gravel turnaround inside the Phase 3 area.


--- page 6 ---
• Constructed cross section: 24 feet of driving surface, asphalt paved to Roadway A pavement structural
section, without curb and gutter or sidewalk; graded shoulders both sides.
• Grade tied to Roadway A at Sta. 10+00 (elevation 2850.75 as constructed) and falls approximately 0.8% to
the north over the 180-ft length.
• Constructed on the Phase 3 parcel with the consent of Callaway Land Partners, as owner of the Phase 3
remainder, under a construction license reflected in the Phase 2 improvement agreement package.

turnaround.

from the south.
• "EMERGENCY / CONSTRUCTION ACCESS ONLY" placard posted on the barricade at the north
terminus.
• Reflective delineators at 50-ft intervals along both edges of the stub.
Status designation.
This element is expressly designated TEMPORARY on the record drawing. It exists to provide the secondary
point of access for Phase 2 during the interval that the Phase 3 parcel remains undeveloped. Removal and
replacement with the Phase 3 improvement package is anticipated at Phase 3 buildout; disposition of the
constructed section at that time will be handled under the Phase 3 improvement plans and is outside the scope
of this record set.

CLARK COUNTY, NEVADA

Issued by:
Clark County Public Works, Development Review Division
PREFACE
The Uniform Unit Cost Schedule is published by Clark County Public Works for use by engineers of record, developers,
and sureties in preparing an engineer's estimate of probable cost for subdivision improvements offered for bonding under
Clark County Code Title 30 and the Uniform Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction Off-Site
Improvements (Clark County Area).
Unit prices set forth in this schedule reflect current Southern Nevada construction market conditions as surveyed by the
Department across the twelve-month period preceding the effective date, drawing on bid tabulations for publicly bid
subdivision and off-site improvement work in unincorporated Clark County and the incorporated municipalities of the Las
Vegas Valley. The schedule is intended to normalize bonding across projects and to remove unit price disputes from the
plan check cycle.
Engineer's estimates for subdivision performance and labor-and-material bonds submitted to Clark County shall use the
unit prices published in this schedule unless project-specific pricing is documented in writing (three qualified
subcontractor quotes or an executed prime contract, dated within ninety (90) days of estimate submittal) and approved by
Clark County Development Review prior to bond posting. Where project-specific pricing is approved, the higher of the
two unit prices shall govern for bonding purposes.
Contingency, mobilization, and design/inspection allowances stated in Section 11 shall be applied to the sum of itemized
construction cost in every engineer's estimate submitted for bonding.
ESCALATION AND REVIEW
This schedule is reviewed annually by the Department. Revised schedules are issued each January, with an effective date
of 01/01 of the calendar year. Between annual issues, the Department may issue a mid-year addendum where documented
market conditions materially depart (±10 percent or greater on any category) from the published unit price. Bonding
accepted against a superseded schedule remains in force at the amount posted; renewals, reissues, and increases occurring
after a schedule effective date shall use the current schedule.
Estimates submitted within thirty (30) days after a schedule effective date may, at the applicant's election, be computed
against the immediately superseded schedule.

## Requested deliverables (exact)
1. Memorandum to Callaway Land Partners, for signature by Max Braddock, dated **10/31/2026**, saved at:
   `/filesystem/Correspondence/Client/Memo_to_Callaway_2026-10-31.docx`
2. The memo must give, in answer-first form:
   - corrected **Section 2 — Storm Drain and Detention** subtotal;
   - a **line-by-line table of every quantity or unit-price change**, with the plan sheet it comes from;
   - the **revised rounded bond figure**.
3. Scope: **Section 2 only**. Other sections are unchanged except that the construction subtotal and final bond must be recomputed.
4. If a plan-shown Section 2 item is missing from the estimate, it must appear in the reconciliation.
5. Price against the Clark County Uniform Unit Cost Schedule effective **01/01/2026**, including Addendum No. 1 effective **03/01/2026**.

7. Flag an item only where the schedule has **nothing matching what the plans show**; leave the amount already carried in the subtotal for flagged items.
8. Where the plans give **no dimension or stationing** for a line item already in the estimate, retain the quantity carried.
9. Round **pipe lengths up to the next whole foot**.

## Hard rules from the record
- Final bonded amount = construction subtotal (Sections 1–8) + Section 9 agreed lump sums; round **up to next $1,000** (Schedule Sec. 12.02; Estimate Cover row 34).
- Section 9: mobilization/bonds/insurance $350,000 and contingency $150,000 are agreed lump sums under Addendum 11.05; item 11.02 design/survey/inspection is owner-carried under 11.06 (Estimate note row 189).

WHEREAS, the Subdivider is the owner and developer of certain real property in the unincorporated

generally located at Rainbow Boulevard and Windmill Lane, Las Vegas, NV 89178, and commonly known as
Desert Sage Ranch (the “Subdivision”);
WHEREAS, the Subdivision consists of approximately 140 acres and is to be developed in phases
pursuant to the tentative map approved by Clark County on March 14, 2022, application number
TM-22-500041 (the “Tentative Map”);
WHEREAS, the Subdivider has caused improvement plans for Phases 1 and 2 of the Subdivision to be
prepared by Sundial Engineering & Survey (NV COA #C-3874) and submitted to and approved by the Director
of Public Works (the “Plans”), consisting of grading and drainage, streets, storm drain, wet and dry utility,
monumentation and offsite improvement sheets required to serve the recorded lots of Phases 1 and 2;

WHEREAS, this Agreement addresses the improvements required for Phase 2 of the Subdivision (the
“Work”), which Work has been separated on the Plans and in the itemized schedule attached hereto as Exhibit
A into (i) offsite improvements and (ii) onsite improvements;
WHEREAS, the County requires, as a condition of approval of the final map for Phase 2 and of the
issuance of an offsite improvement permit and onsite construction permits, that the Subdivider execute this
Agreement and post security in the full amount of the estimated cost of the Work, as more particularly set forth
in Exhibit A hereto;
WHEREAS, concurrently herewith the Subdivider has caused a performance and guaranty bond to be
issued in the penal sum of Three Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars ($3,200,000), Bond No.
SU-2222-2023-Ph2, by AEGIS SURETY COMPANY as Surety, attached hereto and made a part hereof as the
rider following Exhibit A (the “Bond”);
NOW, THEREFORE, for and in consideration of the mutual promises herein contained, the approval of
the Phase 2 final map, and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are
acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:
ARTICLE I. CONSTRUCTION OF THE WORK
1.1   The Subdivider, at its sole cost and expense, and at no cost or expense to the County, shall construct and
complete all of the Work, consisting of both the offsite improvements and the onsite improvements set forth in
the Plans and itemized in Exhibit A, including but not limited to collector road half-improvements, offsite signal
modifications, offsite storm drain trunk connection, internal streets, storm drain, wet and dry utilities, and
monumentation.
1.2   The Work shall be constructed in accordance with the Clark County Code, the Uniform Standard
Specifications for Public Works’ Construction Off-Site Improvements — Clark County Area, the Plans as
approved by the Director of Public Works, any and all permits issued by the County, and other requirements of
the County.
1.3   The Subdivider shall obtain, prior to commencement of any portion of the Work, all required permits,
including but not limited to an offsite improvement permit, onsite construction permits, and permits required by
other local, County, State and Federal agencies.
ARTICLE II. APPROVAL OF PLANS; PRECONDITIONS TO CONSTRUCTION
2.1   No portion of the Work shall commence until:
(a)   The Plans have been approved by the Director of Public Works (“Director”);
(b)   All plan-check and inspection fees required by Title 30 of the Clark County Code have been paid;
(c)   The security required by Article IV has been executed and delivered to the County; and
(d)   All applicable permits have been issued.
ARTICLE III. NOTICE OF COMMENCEMENT AND INSPECTIONS
3.1   The Subdivider shall notify the Director at least twenty-four (24) hours in advance of commencement of
any of the items of Work enumerated in Chapter 30.32 of the Clark County Code, including without limitation
the placing of sewer, water, gas, power, telephone lines and fire hydrants; the backfilling of the same; the
placing of concrete for curb, gutter, sidewalk, valley gutters, storm drain structures, manholes and
street-lighting foundations; the placing of Type I and Type II gravel base course; the priming of base course; the
placing of street lighting; and the placing of street name signs and traffic-control signs.
3.2   The Subdivider shall comply with Chapter 30.32 of the Clark County Code in obtaining inspections of the
Work from the County.

Page 3

ARTICLE IV. SECURITY
4.1   As security for the faithful performance of this Agreement and the completion of the Work, the Subdivider
shall deliver to the County the Bond in the penal sum of $3,200,000, being the aggregate of the offsite subtotal
and the onsite subtotal set forth in Exhibit A.
4.2   The security is furnished pursuant to Title 30 of the Clark County Code and is a condition precedent to
approval of the Phase 2 final map and issuance of the offsite improvement permit and onsite construction
permits.
4.3   The security shall remain in full force and effect until the Work has been accepted by the County pursuant
to Article VI and released pursuant to Article VII, and any warranty period applicable to the accepted Work has
expired.
ARTICLE V. ADJUSTMENT OF UTILITIES; COMPLIANCE
5.1   The Subdivider shall, at its sole cost and expense, make all adjustments to existing utilities necessitated by
the Work.
5.2   The Subdivider shall perform and complete the Work in accordance with the Clark County Code, all
applicable permits, the Plans, and other requirements of the County. The County retains the right to require
corrections at any time before release of the security pursuant to Article VII, even where the Plans have been
previously approved by the Director.
ARTICLE VI. INSPECTION AND ACCEPTANCE
6.1   The Work shall be inspected by the County in accordance with Chapter 30.32 of the Clark County Code.
Ordinarily, no less than one continuous block of any single item of Work will be inspected and approved.
6.2   The offsite improvements and the onsite improvements shall be inspected and processed for acceptance as
separate components. Each component shall be subject to a prefinal and final inspection by the County. Upon
satisfactory completion of the applicable inspections and receipt of any punchlist corrections, the Director of
Public Works, or his designee, may issue a written acceptance of the component. Written acceptance of a
component may occur at different times for the offsite component and the onsite component.
6.3   Inspection or approval of any item of Work, or a portion of the Work, shall not forfeit the right of the
County to require corrections to quality, workmanship or materials at any time prior to written acceptance of the
applicable component, notwithstanding any prior approval issued by oversight.
ARTICLE VII. RELEASE OF SECURITY
7.1   The provisions of this Article VII shall govern the release of the security posted under Article IV and the
Bond attached hereto.
7.2   Release provision. The Subdivider may request in writing partial or full release of the bonded amount
corresponding to any component of the Work upon written acceptance of that component of the Work by Clark
County Public Works. Offsite and onsite improvements shall be treated as separate components and may be
accepted, and their corresponding bond amounts released, independently, upon prefinal and final inspection.
7.3   The bonded amount corresponding to each component of the Work is the subtotal for that component as set
forth in Exhibit A. The offsite component is bonded in the amount of $1,100,000 and the onsite component is
bonded in the amount of $2,100,000, together totaling the penal sum of the Bond.
7.4   A written request for release of security shall reference this Agreement, the Bond number, the recording
instrument number of this Agreement, and the component or components for which release is sought, and shall
attach the County’s written acceptance of the applicable component. The County will process the release in the
ordinary course upon confirmation that the applicable component has been accepted pursuant to Article VI and

that no punchlist items remain outstanding as to that component.
7.5   Any warranty security or maintenance guarantee applicable to accepted Work shall be posted in
accordance with Title 30 of the Clark County Code prior to release of performance security for the applicable
component.
ARTICLE VIII. DEFAULT; REMEDIES
8.1   In the event the Subdivider fails to commence or complete the Work, or any portion of the Work, within
the period allowed by the applicable permit, or is otherwise in default of this Agreement, the County may call
upon the Bond for completion of the Work in accordance with the Plans.
8.2   In the event of a threat or danger to the health, safety or welfare of the public arising from the Subdivider’s
work, as solely determined by the Director, the Subdivider shall, at its sole cost, immediately eliminate the
threat as directed by the County. Upon failure to do so, the County may proceed against the Bond or complete
the Work itself and invoice the Subdivider.
ARTICLE IX. INDEMNITY AND INSURANCE
9.1   The Subdivider shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless the County, its officers, employees and agents
from and against any and all claims, damages, losses and expenses (including reasonable attorneys’ fees) arising
out of or resulting from the Subdivider’s performance of the Work.
9.2   The Subdivider shall maintain commercial general liability insurance with combined single limits of not
less than $2,000,000 per occurrence, and shall name the County as an additional insured, in accordance with the
County’s standard insurance requirements for offsite improvement agreements.
ARTICLE X. GENERAL PROVISIONS
10.1   Recording. This Agreement shall be recorded in the Official Records of the Clark County Recorder and
shall run with the land comprising Phase 2 of the Subdivision.
10.2   Successors. This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the Parties and their
respective successors and assigns.
10.3   Governing law. This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the
State of Nevada, and venue for any action arising hereunder shall lie in Clark County, Nevada.
10.4   Entire agreement. This Agreement, together with Exhibit A and the Bond attached hereto, constitutes
the entire agreement between the Parties with respect to the Phase 2 Work and supersedes all prior negotiations
and understandings.

"""Self-check for the DSR Phase 3 Section 2 reconciliation and bond."""
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP, ROUND_CEILING
import csv, math, json

D=Decimal
def money(x): return D(x).quantize(D('0.01'), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
def dollars(x): return int(D(x).quantize(D('1'), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))

# C-8 / HGL reach data: reach, from, to, station_up, station_down, diameter
reaches = [
    ('R1','S-1','S-2',0.00,213.58,36),
    ('R2','S-2','S-3',213.58,396.65,36),
    ('R3','S-3','S-4',396.65,610.23,36),
    ('R4','S-4','S-5',610.23,869.58,36),
    ('R5','S-5','S-6',869.58,1128.93,48),
    ('R6','S-6','S-7',1128.93,1312.00,48),
    ('R7','S-7','S-8',1312.00,1556.09,48),
    ('R8','S-8','S-9',1556.09,1762.04,60),
    ('R9','S-9','S-10',1762.04,1975.62,60),
    ('R10','S-10','S-11',1975.62,2109.11,60),
    ('R11','S-11','S-12',2109.11,2303.62,60),
    ('R12','S-12','S-13',2303.62,2501.95,60),
    ('R13','S-13','S-14',2501.95,2649.65,60),
    ('R14','S-14','S-15',0.00,240.00,60),
]
pipe = {}
for r in reaches:
    dia=r[5]; length=D(str(r[4]))-D(str(r[3]))
    pipe.setdefault(dia,[]).append((r[0],length))
rounded={}
for dia,vals in pipe.items():
    raw=sum(v for _,v in vals)
    rounded[dia]=int(raw.to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_CEILING))
print('HGL reach lengths by diameter:')
for dia in sorted(pipe):
    print(' ',dia,'in:', ' + '.join(f'{n}={l}' for n,l in pipe[dia]), '=',sum(l for _,l in pipe[dia]),'->',rounded[dia],'LF')
assert rounded=={36:870,48:687,60:1334}, rounded

# Carried Section 2 lines, from Estimate sheet rows 20-32
carried = [
 ('2.04','36-inch RCP, Class III, in trench, complete in place','LF',D('870'),D('172'),'C-8 / HGL R1-R4'),
 ('2.06','48-inch RCP, Class III, in trench, complete in place','LF',D('687'),D('258'),'C-8 / HGL R5-R7'),
 ('2.08','60-inch RCP, Class III, in trench, complete in place','LF',D('1334'),D('372'),'C-8 / HGL R8-R14'),
 ('2.30','Catch basin, Type A, standard curb inlet, depth <= 6 ft','EA',D('12'),D('4850'),'C-8'),
 ('2.34','Drop inlet, area drain','EA',D('2'),D('3900'),'C-8'),
 ('2.35','Storm drain manhole, 48-inch dia., depth <= 8 ft','EA',D('14'),D('6400'),'C-8'),
 ('2.39','Junction structure, cast-in-place, sized per plan','CY',D('60'),D('1150'),'C-8'),
 ('2.40','Headwall, cast-in-place, up to 48-inch pipe','EA',D('2'),D('5400'),'C-8 / C-9'),
 ('2.42','Riprap, D50 = 12 inches, on filter fabric','SY',D('500'),D('86'),'C-9'),
 ('2.44','Detention basin excavation, unclassified material','CY',D('10000'),D('9.75'),'C-6 / C-9'),
 ('2.45','Detention basin outlet structure, per plan','LS',D('1'),D('28000'),'C-9'),
 ('2.46','Detention basin fencing, 6-ft chain link with 3-strand barbed','LF',D('1400'),D('34'),'C-6 / C-9'),
 ('2.99','Field connections to Phase 2 storm outfall structure and adjustments, allowance','LS',D('1'),D('2300'),'C-6 / C-8'),
]
corr = {
 '2.30': {'qty':D('9'), 'price':D('4850'), 'note':'C-8 schedules 9 curb inlets; 3 fewer than carried.'},
 '2.35': {'qty':D('14'), 'price':D('8750'), 'note':'C-8 requires 5-ft (60-in) manholes; use schedule 2.36.'},
}
new = [
 ('2.03','30-inch RCP, Class III, in trench, complete in place (basin outlet to existing stub)','LF',D('100'),D('138'),'C-9 / C-6'),
]

rows=[]
carried_total=D('0')
for item,desc,unit,qty,price,src in carried:
    ext=money(qty*price); carried_total+=ext
    q2=corr.get(item,{}).get('qty',qty); p2=corr.get(item,{}).get('price',price)
    ext2=money(q2*p2)
    rows.append(dict(item=item,description=desc,unit=unit,qty_carried=qty,qty_corrected=q2,
        price_carried=price,price_corrected=p2,ext_carried=ext,ext_corrected=ext2,
        delta=ext2-ext,source=src,note=corr.get(item,{}).get('note','Reviewed; retained.')))
for item,desc,unit,qty,price,src in new:
    ext2=money(qty*price)
    rows.append(dict(item=item,description=desc,unit=unit,qty_carried=D('0'),qty_corrected=qty,
        price_carried=D('0'),price_corrected=price,ext_carried=D('0'),ext_corrected=ext2,
        delta=ext2,source=src,note='Plan-shown 30-in RCP outlet missing from estimate; length = (2851.00-2850.75)/0.0025 = 100 LF.'))

corrected_total=sum((r['ext_corrected'] for r in rows),D('0'))
delta_total=sum((r['delta'] for r in rows),D('0'))
print('\nCarried Section 2 subtotal:',carried_total)
print('Corrected Section 2 subtotal:',corrected_total)
print('Net delta:',delta_total)
assert carried_total==D('1276934.00'), carried_total
assert corrected_total-carried_total==delta_total, (corrected_total,carried_total,delta_total)
assert delta_total==D('32150.00'), delta_total

# Whole-estimate recomputation
construction_carried=D('4856565.75')
other_sections=construction_carried-carried_total
allowances=D('350000')+D('150000')
construction_corrected=other_sections+corrected_total
grand=construction_corrected+allowances
bond=int((grand/D('1000')).to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_CEILING))*1000
print('Other Sections 1,3-8 (unchanged):',other_sections)
print('Corrected construction subtotal:',construction_corrected)
print('Section 9 allowances:',allowances)
print('Grand total unrounded:',grand)
print('Rounded bond:',bond)
assert construction_corrected==D('4888715.75'), construction_corrected
assert grand==D('5388715.75'), grand
assert bond==5389000, bond

# write CSV
with open('reconciliation.csv','w',newline='',encoding='utf-8') as f:
    w=csv.writer(f)
    w.writerow(['item','description','unit','qty_carried','qty_corrected','price_carried','price_corrected','ext_carried','ext_corrected','delta','source','note'])
    for r in rows:
        w.writerow([r[k] for k in ['item','description','unit','qty_carried','qty_corrected','price_carried','price_corrected','ext_carried','ext_corrected','delta','source','note']])
    w.writerow(['','SECTION 2 SUBTOTAL','','','','','',carried_total,'',delta_total,'',''])
print('\nWrote reconciliation.csv; all assertions passed.')

171:## Bottom line
memo's row arithmetic ($1,276,934 − $14,550 + $32,900 + $13,800 = $1,309,084) is correct for its stated assumptions;
Sections 1 and 3–8 sum to $3,579,631.75; the grand total $5,388,715.75 rounds to $5,389,000. The pipe takeoff from
C-8 stations is correct: 869.58 → 870 LF, 686.51 → 687 LF, and 1,333.56 → 1,334 LF (including 240 LF R14). The
30-inch outlet length is correctly 100 LF from (2,851.00 − 2,850.75)/0.0025. These findings are favourable and do not
offset Findings 1–4.

## Bottom line

The memo's $1,309,084 / $5,389,000 cannot be accepted as the corrected Section 2 result. The minimum clear error is
the 2.35 quantity (10 manholes, not 14): that alone gives **$1,274,084** and a **$5,354,000** bond. Adding the
schedule-required depth items gives **$1,311,221.95** / **$5,391,000** if the Type A substitution is accepted; if the
C-8 Type G requirement is honoured under the “flag, don't invent a price” rule, the 2.30 carried amount stays and the
result is **$1,303,717.70** / **$5,384,000**. The 2.44 basin excavation is a further potential **+$28,655**, and the
access ramp is a further **+$2,107**. The corrected subtotal must be recomputed after the Type G/Type A, 2.44 and ramp
questions are resolved; it is not $1,309,084.

# Independent review — DSR Phase 3 Section 2 estimate / memo to Callaway

Reviewer: independent checking engineer. Deliverables reviewed but not modified:
`/filesystem/Correspondence/Client/Memo_to_Callaway_2026-10-31.docx` (DOCX, 6 pages), and the Section 2 figures in
`/filesystem/Cost Estimates/DSR_Ph3_Engineers_Estimate.xlsx`.

Sources checked directly: `Design-Drafting/Phase 3/DSR_Ph3_Improvement_Plans_C1-C9.pdf` (C-6 p.11, C-8 pp.13–15,
C-9 pp.15–18), `Cost Estimates/CC_Unit_Cost_Schedule.pdf` (effective 01/01/2026 + Addendum No. 1),
`Reports-Studies/DSR_Ph3_StormDrain_HGL.xlsx`, `Correspondence/Agency/TM-22-500041_Conditions_of_Approval_03142022.pdf`,
and the estimate itself. I recomputed the Section 2 extensions, station-derived pipe lengths, subtotal, construction
subtotal and bond with Decimal arithmetic. The author's arithmetic is internally consistent, but the quantities and
the catch-basin pricing basis are not.

## Findings

### 1. MAJOR — Item 2.35 manhole quantity is 14 EA; the plans show 10 manholes, not 14.
**Requirement / basis.** Instruction: check Section 2 against “what's actually on the plans”; the estimate's own 2.35
description is a storm-drain manhole. C-8 Structure Schedule (pp.13–14) gives the type of every S-structure.

**What the deliverable has.** Memo §3 and Attachment A: 2.35 corrected to 14 EA at the 60-inch price $8,750 =
$122,500. Memo §3 says “the 14-EA count is the 14 S-structures and is retained because C-8 does not give a separate
manhole count.”

**What it should be.** C-8 does give a separate count by type:
- manhole only: S-1, S-7, S-10, S-11, S-14 = 5;
- curb inlet **+ junction manhole**: S-2, S-4, S-6, S-8, S-12 = 5;
- curb inlet only: S-3, S-5, S-9, S-13 = 4.
Total = 14 structures, but only **10 manholes** on the face of the type column. The four “Curb inlet” structures
(S-3, S-5, S-9, S-13) are already counted in 2.30 and are not labelled as containing a manhole; the memo has not shown
that a Type G curb inlet includes a 5-ft manhole. If the County confirms that every curb inlet also contains a manhole,
14 could be defended; on the issued plan the type column supports 10. The memo's own list of nine curb inlets includes
five structures that also contain a junction manhole (S-2, S-4, S-6, S-8, S-12); it then counts every one of the 14
structures again as a manhole.

**Correct 2.35 (base item only):** 10 × $8,750 = **$87,500**, not $122,500. Change from carried = −$2,100, not
+$32,900. With only this correction, Section 2 = $1,276,934 − $14,550 (2.30) − $2,100 (2.35) + $13,800 (2.03) =
**$1,274,084**, and the bond would be ceiling(($3,579,631.75 + $1,274,084 + $500,000)/1,000)×1,000 =
**$5,354,000**. The memo's $1,309,084 / $5,389,000 are therefore overstated by $35,000 / $35,000 relative to this
minimum correction.

**Evidence.** C-8 Structure Schedule, S-1 through S-14 (PDF pp.13–14): “S-1 5' dia. manhole (headwall/cleanout)”;
S-3, S-5, S-9, S-13 “Curb inlet”; S-7, S-10, S-11, S-14 “Junction manhole”; S-2, S-4, S-6, S-8, S-12 “Curb inlet +
junction manhole.” C-8 Design Note p.15: “All manholes are 5-foot inside diameter unless noted otherwise.”

### 2. MAJOR — The 60-inch manhole and catch-basin depth adders (2.38 and 2.31) are omitted; several structures are deeper than the schedule base depth.
**Requirement / basis.** Uniform Unit Cost Schedule items 2.31 (“Catch basin, Type A, depth > 6 ft, per additional ft”,
$475/VF) and 2.38 (“Storm drain manhole additional depth beyond schedule, per foot”, $685/VF). The C-8 schedule gives
rim and invert-out elevations, so depth is a plan dimension, not a missing dimension.

**What the deliverable has.** 2.35 is priced at the 60-inch base item for “depth ≤ 10 ft” with no 2.38 addition; 2.30 is
priced at the Type A base item for “depth ≤ 6 ft” with no 2.31 addition (Requirements register REQ022 and REQ025
expressly say “Not applied”; the instruction contains no such exemption).

**What it should be.** Using depth = rim − invert out from the C-8 table:
- Nine curb inlets, depth 7.77 to 15.31 ft; additional depth over 6 ft = 46.43 VF; 2.31 addition = 46.43 × $475 =
  **$22,054.25**. Correct 2.30 (9 EA) = $43,650 + $22,054.25 = **$65,704.25**.
- Ten manholes, depth 7.00 to 15.74 ft; additional depth over 10 ft = 22.02 VF; 2.38 addition = 22.02 × $685 =
  **$15,083.70**. Correct 2.35 (10 EA) = $87,500 + $15,083.70 = **$102,583.70**.
- With both depth additions (and the corrected 10 manholes), Section 2 = $1,276,934 − $58,200 + $65,704.25 −
  $89,600 + $102,583.70 + $13,800 = **$1,311,221.95**; bond = **$5,391,000**.
If the memo's 14-EA count is accepted, the 2.38 addition is still required for S-9 (2.77 VF) and S-13 (5.31 VF) plus the
22.02 VF above, or 30.10 VF × $685 = $20,618.50, making 2.35 $143,118.50 and Section 2 $1,329,702.50 (bond
$5,410,000). Either way the memo's $1,309,084 is below the schedule-required figure; it is not a conservative
estimate.

**Evidence.** C-8 schedule rim/invert values: e.g. S-6 rim 2,876.10 / invert out 2,865.39 = 10.71 ft; S-8 2,874.94 −
2,862.86 = 12.08 ft; S-14 2,872.10 − 2,856.36 = 15.74 ft; S-13 2,872.55 − 2,857.24 = 15.31 ft. Schedule items 2.31 and
2.38, p.3.

### 3. MAJOR — The catch-basin line was re-priced as Type A and reduced from 12 to 9, but C-8 requires Type G; the C-9 “Detail 1 Type A” cited in the memo is not in the issued C-9.
**Requirement / basis.** Instruction: “Flag an item only where the schedule has nothing matching what the plans show,
and leave the amount already carried in the subtotal for anything you flag.” C-8 Storm Drain Design Notes p.15:
“Curb inlets are Type G with 8-foot opening per Clark County Standard Drawing SD-305.”

**What the deliverable has.** Memo §3 and the cross-check note: “C-9 Detail 1 says Type A per CCUSD 411. The schedule
has no Type G item, so Type A item 2.30 is used for the nine C-8 curb inlets.” 2.30 is changed 12 → 9 EA, −$14,550.

**What it should be.** The issued C-9 (pp.16–18) contains the storage table, Sections A–A′/B–B′, spillway, outlet
structure and access-ramp details; it contains **no catch-basin Detail 1** and no Type A callout. The only plan
statement on catch-basin type is C-8's Type G. The schedule has no Type G item. On the documents actually issued, 2.30
therefore has no schedule match and must be flagged; the carried 12 × $4,850 = **$58,200** stays in the subtotal under
the instruction. The memo's −$14,550 is not authorised, and the internal QA/QC checklist's reference to “Detail 1/C-9”
does not make that detail part of the issued plan set. If the County confirms a Type A substitution in writing, the 9
EA price still needs the 2.31 depth addition (Finding 2); but the memo has not obtained that confirmation.

**Evidence.** C-8 p.15 (“Curb inlets are Type G…”); C-9 pp.16–18 (no catch-basin detail); memo Attachment A p.6
cross-check note; `DSR_Ph3_QAQC_Checklist.xlsx` row 24 (the only place “Detail 1/C-9” is asserted).

### 4. MAJOR (bond basis) — The memo presents $5,389,000 as the revised bond while dismissing the 11.04 escalation reserve on a false premise and admitting the Section 9 lump sums have no executed 11.05 agreement.
**Requirement / basis.** Addendum No. 1 item 11.05 requires lump sums to be **agreed** by the subdivider and the
Department; item 11.04 requires a 3.0%/year escalation reserve “where bond term exceeds 24 months.” Conditions of
Approval, Public Works condition 9, requires final acceptance after a **two-year maintenance period**, and the Phase 2
SIA (Art. 4.3) keeps security in force until acceptance and any warranty period expires.

**What the deliverable has.** Memo §7: “No escalation reserve under 11.04 is applied because the record does not
establish a bond term beyond 24 months”; the memo later says “The provided record contains no separate executed
agreement; confirm the County's written agreement before posting. The $5,389,000 bond assumes those lump sums stand.”

**What it should be.** The record does establish a two-year maintenance period after completion (Conditions of
Approval condition 9; Phase 2 SIA Art. 4.3 keeps security until acceptance and warranty expiry), so the bond term from
posting to release is construction time plus 24 months — i.e. it exceeds 24 months. If 11.04 applies, a 3% reserve on
the corrected construction subtotal (about $146,600 on $4.89M) is required for each year beyond 24 months; the memo's
figure would be understated. Separately, absent an executed 11.05 agreement the default 5% + 8% + 10% Section 11
allowances would produce a much larger bond than $5,389,000. The memo's own caveat means $5,389,000 is not a definite
bond figure; it is conditional on a document not in the record. This is outside Section 2 but is directly material to
the requested bond answer.

**Evidence.** Conditions of Approval p.3 condition 9 (“two-year maintenance period”); Addendum No. 1 pp.11; Phase 2 SIA
Art. 4.3 p.3; memo §7 and cross-check note p.6.

### 5. MAJOR — The 2.44 detention-basin excavation quantity is not supported by the plan geometry; 10,000 CY is the 6.4 ac-ft storage figure, not the excavated volume to top of berm.
**Requirement / basis.** Instruction: where the plans give no dimension or stationing, the carried quantity stands.
C-6/C-9 do give basin dimensions and a contour-area storage table, so this is not a “no dimension” item.

**What the deliverable has.** 2.44 retained at 10,000 CY / $97,500, with the reason “C-6/C-9 give the 6.4 ac-ft
allocation and basin geometry but no excavation quantity or stationing; carried quantity stands.”

**What it should be.** C-9 Storage Summary tabulates areas from 29,450 sf at elevation 2,851.00 to 57,180 sf at top of
berm 2,859.20 and a structural volume of 8.02 ac-ft. 8.02 ac-ft × 43,560 / 27 = **12,939 CY**. Average-end-area over the
same 8.20 ft, (29,450 + 57,180)/2 × 8.20 / 27 = **13,155 CY**. The carried 10,000 CY is approximately 6.4 ac-ft ×
43,560 / 27 = 10,325 CY — the storage allocation, not the basin excavation. At $9.75/CY, correcting to 12,939 CY adds
**$28,655.25** (to 13,155 CY adds $30,761). If the top 1.29 ft of the basin is built berm fill rather than cut, the
6.4 ac-ft/10,325 CY figure could be the correct cut volume; but the memo does not say that, and it describes the
10,000 CY as excavation using the 6.4 ac-ft allocation. The plan does give the dimensions needed to measure it, so the
“no dimension/stationing” reason is not sufficient.

**Evidence.** C-9 Storage Summary table pp.16; C-6 basin callouts p.11 (top of berm 2,859.20, bottom 2,851.00, top area
≈1.31 ac); C-9 basin notes p.18 (8.02 ac-ft structural volume to top of berm). The 6.4 ac-ft is the allocation to the
100-year WSE, not the total excavation. The open CC-PW comment G-3 (basin volume reconciliation) is also omitted from
the memo's list of outstanding items, and the 09/25/2026 preliminary detention calculation (`DSR_Ph3_Detention_Calc_prelim.xlsx`)
reports a required volume of 8.1 ac-ft, not 6.4 — another reason the 10,000 CY / 6.4 ac-ft basis needs reconciliation.

### 6. MINOR — The basin access ramp was flagged as having no schedule match, but schedule item 3.05 (6-inch aggregate base) matches the ramp surface and the ramp quantity is measurable.
**Requirement / basis.** Instruction: “Flag an item only where the schedule has nothing matching what the plans show.” C-6/C-9: ramp 15 ft wide, 6% grade from top of berm 2,859.20 to basin bottom 2,851.00, surface 6-inch aggregate base course.

**What the deliverable has.** Memo §5, Table 4: access ramp “2,050 SF = 227.8 SY”; “2.47 is an access ramp but includes 4-in AC over 6-in aggregate base at $32.00/SY; the plan shows 6-in aggregate base only”; amount added $0. The memo says the closest analogue (2.47) would add about $7,300.

**What it should be.** Schedule item 3.05 is “Aggregate base course, Type II, 6-inch thickness” at **$9.25/SY**, which is exactly the ramp surface specified; the 2.47 item is not the closest match. 8.20 ft / 0.06 = 136.67 LF; 136.67 × 15 = 2,050 SF = 227.8 SY; 227.8 × $9.25 = **$2,107.43**. The ramp is a Section 2 detention-basin appurtenance, so this belongs in the Section 2 reconciliation even though the unit price sits in schedule Section 3. The memo's “no exact match” conclusion is wrong; at most it should explain why it declines to use 3.05.

**Evidence.** C-9 Access Ramp detail p.18; C-6 p.11 (“ramp surface to be 6-inch aggregate base course”); schedule item 3.05 p.3; memo Table 4 p.3.

### 7. MINOR — The memo misstates the C-9 spillway freeboard conflict and resolves it to the wrong value.
**Requirement / basis.** C-9 p.17 says weir crest 2,858.50 is “0.71′ above 100-year water surface”; C-9 p.18 says
“0.60′ above the 100-year water surface.” The tabulated 100-year WSE is 2,857.91, so 2,858.50 − 2,857.91 = **0.59 ft**.

**What the deliverable has.** Cross-check note p.6: “C-9 gives 0.71 ft in one callout and 0.60 ft in the basin notes;
the tabulated difference from 2,857.91 ft is 0.59 ft. No cost impact on the flagged ACB; correct the note at
resubmittal.”

**What it should be.** The memo correctly notices the inconsistency but does not state that both callouts are wrong;
it should say the governing value is 0.59 ft and require both callouts to be corrected. This does not change the
Section 2 cost but is an unresolved plan-note conflict that a reviewer should not leave as “0.71 or 0.60.”

**Evidence.** C-9 pp.17–18; C-6 p.11 WSE 2,857.91.

### 8. MINOR — The memo over-applies the “no dimension or stationing” instruction to items that are not shown on C-6/C-8/C-9 at all (notably 2.34 drop inlets and 2.46 fencing).
**Requirement / basis.** Instruction: “Where the plans give no dimension or stationing for a line item already in the
estimate, the quantity already carried stands.” That clause preserves a quantity for an item that is shown but not
dimensioned; it does not establish a plan basis for an item that is absent.

**What the deliverable has.** 2.34 “Drop inlet, area drain” 2 EA $7,800 and 2.46 “Detention basin fencing” 1,400 LF
$47,600 are retained with the reason “no dimension or stationing.”

**What it should be.** C-8 shows nine curb inlets and no area drains; C-6/C-9 show a vehicle gate but no perimeter
fence length. These lines should be flagged as “no plan basis — retained per instruction only if the County accepts
the carried allowance,” or a plan basis should be identified. This is a reconciliation completeness issue; the
instruction does not expressly direct removal, so the amounts need not be changed, but the memo should not present
“no dimension” as the reason without saying the items are not depicted.

**Evidence.** C-8 schedule pp.13–14 (types; no area drain); C-9 p.18 (gate only); memo Attachment A table 5 rows
2.34/2.46.

### 9. MINOR — Arithmetic and format checks that pass.
The DOCX opens, has 6 pages, and `ahpele_check.py` reports no problems. The filename, date (10/31/2026), addressee,
signature block and the three requested answers are present. Section 2 carried extensions sum to $1,276,934; the
memo's row arithmetic ($1,276,934 − $14,550 + $32,900 + $13,800 = $1,309,084) is correct for its stated assumptions;
Sections 1 and 3–8 sum to $3,579,631.75; the grand total $5,388,715.75 rounds to $5,389,000. The pipe takeoff from
C-8 stations is correct: 869.58 → 870 LF, 686.51 → 687 LF, and 1,333.56 → 1,334 LF (including 240 LF R14). The
30-inch outlet length is correctly 100 LF from (2,851.00 − 2,850.75)/0.0025. These findings are favourable and do not
offset Findings 1–4.

## Bottom line

The memo's $1,309,084 / $5,389,000 cannot be accepted as the corrected Section 2 result. The minimum clear error is
the 2.35 quantity (10 manholes, not 14): that alone gives **$1,274,084** and a **$5,354,000** bond. Adding the
schedule-required depth items gives **$1,311,221.95** / **$5,391,000** if the Type A substitution is accepted; if the
C-8 Type G requirement is honoured under the “flag, don't invent a price” rule, the 2.30 carried amount stays and the
result is **$1,303,717.70** / **$5,384,000**. The 2.44 basin excavation is a further potential **+$28,655**, and the
access ramp is a further **+$2,107**. The corrected subtotal must be recomputed after the Type G/Type A, 2.44 and ramp
questions are resolved; it is not $1,309,084. The $5,389,000 bond also assumes no 11.04 escalation reserve; the
two-year maintenance period in the Conditions makes that assumption doubtful, so the final bond figure is not settled.

# Independent review — DSR Phase 3 Section 2 estimate / memo to Callaway

Reviewer: independent checking engineer. Deliverables reviewed but not modified:
`/filesystem/Correspondence/Client/Memo_to_Callaway_2026-10-31.docx` (DOCX, 6 pages), and the Section 2 figures in
`/filesystem/Cost Estimates/DSR_Ph3_Engineers_Estimate.xlsx`.

Sources checked directly: `Design-Drafting/Phase 3/DSR_Ph3_Improvement_Plans_C1-C9.pdf` (C-6 p.11, C-8 pp.13–15,
C-9 pp.15–18), `Cost Estimates/CC_Unit_Cost_Schedule.pdf` (effective 01/01/2026 + Addendum No. 1),
`Reports-Studies/DSR_Ph3_StormDrain_HGL.xlsx`, `Correspondence/Agency/TM-22-500041_Conditions_of_Approval_03142022.pdf`,
and the estimate itself. I recomputed the Section 2 extensions, station-derived pipe lengths, subtotal, construction
subtotal and bond with Decimal arithmetic. The author's arithmetic is internally consistent, but the quantities and
the catch-basin pricing basis are not.

## Findings

### 1. MAJOR — Item 2.35 manhole quantity is 14 EA; the plans show 10 manholes, not 14.
**Requirement / basis.** Instruction: check Section 2 against “what's actually on the plans”; the estimate's own 2.35
description is a storm-drain manhole. C-8 Structure Schedule (pp.13–14) gives the type of every S-structure.

**What the deliverable has.** Memo §3 and Attachment A: 2.35 corrected to 14 EA at the 60-inch price $8,750 =
$122,500. Memo §3 says “the 14-EA count is the 14 S-structures and is retained because C-8 does not give a separate
manhole count.”

**What it should be.** C-8 does give a separate count by type:
- manhole only: S-1, S-7, S-10, S-11, S-14 = 5;
- curb inlet **+ junction manhole**: S-2, S-4, S-6, S-8, S-12 = 5;
- curb inlet only: S-3, S-5, S-9, S-13 = 4.
Total = 14 structures, but only **10 manholes** on the face of the type column. The four “Curb inlet” structures
(S-3, S-5, S-9, S-13) are already counted in 2.30 and are not labelled as containing a manhole; the memo has not shown
that a Type G curb inlet includes a 5-ft manhole. If the County confirms that every curb inlet also contains a manhole,
14 could be defended; on the issued plan the type column supports 10. The memo's own list of nine curb inlets includes
five structures that also contain a junction manhole (S-2, S-4, S-6, S-8, S-12); it then counts every one of the 14
structures again as a manhole.

**Correct 2.35 (base item only):** 10 × $8,750 = **$87,500**, not $122,500. Change from carried = −$2,100, not
+$32,900. With only this correction, Section 2 = $1,276,934 − $14,550 (2.30) − $2,100 (2.35) + $13,800 (2.03) =
