junction manhole.” C-8 Design Note p.15: “All manholes are 5-foot inside diameter unless noted otherwise.”

### 2. MAJOR — The 60-inch manhole and catch-basin depth adders (2.38 and 2.31) are omitted; several structures are deeper than the schedule base depth.
**Requirement / basis.** Uniform Unit Cost Schedule items 2.31 (“Catch basin, Type A, depth > 6 ft, per additional ft”,
$475/VF) and 2.38 (“Storm drain manhole additional depth beyond schedule, per foot”, $685/VF). The C-8 schedule gives
rim and invert-out elevations, so depth is a plan dimension, not a missing dimension.

**What the deliverable has.** 2.35 is priced at the 60-inch base item for “depth ≤ 10 ft” with no 2.38 addition; 2.30 is
priced at the Type A base item for “depth ≤ 6 ft” with no 2.31 addition (Requirements register REQ022 and REQ025
expressly say “Not applied”; the instruction contains no such exemption).

**What it should be.** Using depth = rim − invert out from the C-8 table:
- Nine curb inlets, depth 7.77 to 15.31 ft; additional depth over 6 ft = 46.43 VF; 2.31 addition = 46.43 × $475 =
  **$22,054.25**. Correct 2.30 (9 EA) = $43,650 + $22,054.25 = **$65,704.25**.
- Ten manholes, depth 7.00 to 15.74 ft; additional depth over 10 ft = 22.02 VF; 2.38 addition = 22.02 × $685 =
  **$15,083.70**. Correct 2.35 (10 EA) = $87,500 + $15,083.70 = **$102,583.70**.
- With both depth additions (and the corrected 10 manholes), Section 2 = $1,276,934 − $58,200 + $65,704.25 −
  $89,600 + $102,583.70 + $13,800 = **$1,311,221.95**; bond = **$5,391,000**.
If the memo's 14-EA count is accepted, the 2.38 addition is still required for S-9 (2.77 VF) and S-13 (5.31 VF) plus the

$5,410,000). Either way the memo's $1,309,084 is below the schedule-required figure; it is not a conservative
estimate.

**Evidence.** C-8 schedule rim/invert values: e.g. S-6 rim 2,876.10 / invert out 2,865.39 = 10.71 ft; S-8 2,874.94 −
2,862.86 = 12.08 ft; S-14 2,872.10 − 2,856.36 = 15.74 ft; S-13 2,872.55 − 2,857.24 = 15.31 ft. Schedule items 2.31 and

### 3. MAJOR — The catch-basin line was re-priced as Type A and reduced from 12 to 9, but C-8 requires Type G; the C-9 “Detail 1 Type A” cited in the memo is not in the issued C-9.

**What it should be.** The issued C-9 (pp.16–18) contains the storage table, Sections A–A′/B–B′, spillway, outlet
structure and access-ramp details; it contains **no catch-basin Detail 1** and no Type A callout. The only plan
statement on catch-basin type is C-8's Type G. The schedule has no Type G item. On the documents actually issued, 2.30
therefore has no schedule match and must be flagged; the carried 12 × $4,850 = **$58,200** stays in the subtotal under

does not make that detail part of the issued plan set. If the County confirms a Type A substitution in writing, the 9
EA price still needs the 2.31 depth addition (Finding 2); but the memo has not obtained that confirmation.

**Evidence.** C-8 p.15 (“Curb inlets are Type G…”); C-9 pp.16–18 (no catch-basin detail); memo Attachment A p.6

### 4. MAJOR (bond basis) — The memo presents $5,389,000 as the revised bond while dismissing the 11.04 escalation reserve on a false premise and admitting the Section 9 lump sums have no executed 11.05 agreement.
**Requirement / basis.** Addendum No. 1 item 11.05 requires lump sums to be **agreed** by the subdivider and the
Department; item 11.04 requires a 3.0%/year escalation reserve “where bond term exceeds 24 months.” Conditions of
Approval, Public Works condition 9, requires final acceptance after a **two-year maintenance period**, and the Phase 2
SIA (Art. 4.3) keeps security in force until acceptance and any warranty period expires.

**What the deliverable has.** Memo §7: “No escalation reserve under 11.04 is applied because the record does not
establish a bond term beyond 24 months”; the memo later says “The provided record contains no separate executed
agreement; confirm the County's written agreement before posting. The $5,389,000 bond assumes those lump sums stand.”

**What it should be.** The record does establish a two-year maintenance period after completion (Conditions of
Approval condition 9; Phase 2 SIA Art. 4.3 keeps security until acceptance and warranty expiry), so the bond term from
posting to release is construction time plus 24 months — i.e. it exceeds 24 months. If 11.04 applies, a 3% reserve on
the corrected construction subtotal (about $146,600 on $4.89M) is required for each year beyond 24 months; the memo's
figure would be understated. Separately, absent an executed 11.05 agreement the default 5% + 8% + 10% Section 11
allowances would produce a much larger bond than $5,389,000. The memo's own caveat means $5,389,000 is not a definite
bond figure; it is conditional on a document not in the record. This is outside Section 2 but is directly material to
the requested bond answer.

**Evidence.** Conditions of Approval p.3 condition 9 (“two-year maintenance period”); Addendum No. 1 pp.11; Phase 2 SIA
Art. 4.3 p.3; memo §7 and cross-check note p.6.

### 5. MINOR — The 2.44 detention-basin excavation quantity is not reconciled to the plan geometry; 10,000 CY is the 6.4 ac-ft storage figure, and the C-9 structural volume to top of berm is 8.02 ac-ft.
**Requirement / basis.** Instruction: where the plans give no dimension or stationing, the carried quantity stands.
C-6/C-9 do give basin dimensions and a contour-area storage table, so this is not a “no dimension” item.

**What the deliverable has.** 2.44 retained at 10,000 CY / $97,500, with the reason “C-6/C-9 give the 6.4 ac-ft
allocation and basin geometry but no excavation quantity or stationing; carried quantity stands.”

**What it should be.** C-9 Storage Summary tabulates areas from 29,450 sf at elevation 2,851.00 to 57,180 sf at top of
berm 2,859.20 and a structural volume of 8.02 ac-ft. 8.02 ac-ft × 43,560 / 27 = **12,939 CY**. Average-end-area over the
same 8.20 ft, (29,450 + 57,180)/2 × 8.20 / 27 = **13,155 CY**. The carried 10,000 CY is approximately 6.4 ac-ft ×
43,560 / 27 = 10,325 CY — the storage allocation, not the basin excavation. At $9.75/CY, correcting to 12,939 CY adds
**$28,655.25** (to 13,155 CY adds $30,761). If the top 1.29 ft of the basin is built berm fill rather than cut, the
6.4 ac-ft/10,325 CY figure could be the correct cut volume; but the memo does not say that, and it describes the
10,000 CY as excavation using the 6.4 ac-ft allocation. The plan does give the dimensions needed to measure it, so the
“no dimension/stationing” reason is not sufficient.

**Evidence.** C-9 Storage Summary table pp.16; C-6 basin callouts p.11 (top of berm 2,859.20, bottom 2,851.00, top area
≈1.31 ac); C-9 basin notes p.18 (8.02 ac-ft structural volume to top of berm). The 6.4 ac-ft is the allocation to the
100-year WSE, not the total excavation. The open CC-PW comment G-3 (basin volume reconciliation) is also omitted from
the memo's list of outstanding items, and the 09/25/2026 preliminary detention calculation (`DSR_Ph3_Detention_Calc_prelim.xlsx`)
reports a required volume of 8.1 ac-ft, not 6.4 — another reason the 10,000 CY / 6.4 ac-ft basis needs reconciliation.

### 6. MINOR — The basin access ramp was flagged as having no schedule match, but schedule item 3.05 (6-inch aggregate base) matches the ramp surface and the ramp quantity is measurable.
**Requirement / basis.** Instruction: “Flag an item only where the schedule has nothing matching what the plans show.” C-6/C-9: ramp 15 ft wide, 6% grade from top of berm 2,859.20 to basin bottom 2,851.00, surface 6-inch aggregate base course.

**What it should be.** Schedule item 3.05 is “Aggregate base course, Type II, 6-inch thickness” at **$9.25/SY**, which is exactly the ramp surface specified; the 2.47 item is not the closest match. 8.20 ft / 0.06 = 136.67 LF; 136.67 × 15 = 2,050 SF = 227.78 SY; 227.78 × $9.25 = **$2,106.94**. The memo's “no exact match” conclusion is wrong; at most it should explain why it declines to use 3.05.

### 8. MINOR — The memo over-applies the “no dimension or stationing” instruction to items that are not shown on C-6/C-8/C-9 at all (notably 2.34 drop inlets and 2.46 fencing).

fence length. These lines should be flagged as “no plan basis — retained per instruction only if the County accepts
the carried allowance,” or a plan basis should be identified. This is a reconciliation completeness issue; the
instruction does not expressly direct removal, so the amounts need not be changed, but the memo should not present

### 9. MINOR — Arithmetic and format checks that pass.
The DOCX opens, has 6 pages, and `ahpele_check.py` reports no problems. The filename, date (10/31/2026), addressee,

## Bottom line

The memo's $1,309,084 / $5,389,000 cannot be accepted as the corrected Section 2 result. The minimum clear error is
the 2.35 quantity (10 manholes, not 14): that alone gives **$1,274,084** and a **$5,354,000** bond. Adding the
schedule-required depth items gives **$1,311,221.95** / **$5,391,000** if the Type A substitution is accepted; if the
C-8 Type G requirement is honoured under the “flag, don't invent a price” rule, the 2.30 carried amount stays and the
result is **$1,303,717.70** / **$5,384,000**. The 2.44 basin excavation is a further potential **+$28,655**, and the
access ramp is a further **+$2,107**. The corrected subtotal must be recomputed after the Type G/Type A, 2.44 and ramp
questions are resolved; it is not $1,309,084. The $5,389,000 bond also assumes no 11.04 escalation reserve; the
two-year maintenance period in the Conditions makes that assumption doubtful, so the final bond figure is not settled.

exit_code=0
# Independent review — DSR Phase 3 Section 2 estimate / memo to Callaway

Reviewer: independent checking engineer. Deliverables reviewed but not modified:
`/filesystem/Correspondence/Client/Memo_to_Callaway_2026-10-31.docx` (DOCX, 6 pages), and the Section 2 figures in
`/filesystem/Cost Estimates/DSR_Ph3_Engineers_Estimate.xlsx`.

Sources checked directly: `Design-Drafting/Phase 3/DSR_Ph3_Improvement_Plans_C1-C9.pdf` (C-6 p.11, C-8 pp.13–15,
C-9 pp.15–18), `Cost Estimates/CC_Unit_Cost_Schedule.pdf` (effective 01/01/2026 + Addendum No. 1),
`Reports-Studies/DSR_Ph3_StormDrain_HGL.xlsx`, `Correspondence/Agency/TM-22-500041_Conditions_of_Approval_03142022.pdf`,
and the estimate itself. I recomputed the Section 2 extensions, station-derived pipe lengths, subtotal, construction
subtotal and bond with Decimal arithmetic. The author's arithmetic is internally consistent, but the quantities and
the catch-basin pricing basis are not.

## Findings

### 1. MAJOR — Item 2.35 manhole quantity is 14 EA; the plans show 10 manholes, not 14.
**Requirement / basis.** Instruction: check Section 2 against “what's actually on the plans”; the estimate's own 2.35
description is a storm-drain manhole. C-8 Structure Schedule (pp.13–14) gives the type of every S-structure.

**What the deliverable has.** Memo §3 and Attachment A: 2.35 corrected to 14 EA at the 60-inch price $8,750 =
$122,500. Memo §3 says “the 14-EA count is the 14 S-structures and is retained because C-8 does not give a separate
manhole count.”

**What it should be.** C-8 does give a separate count by type:
- manhole only: S-1, S-7, S-10, S-11, S-14 = 5;
- curb inlet **+ junction manhole**: S-2, S-4, S-6, S-8, S-12 = 5;
- curb inlet only: S-3, S-5, S-9, S-13 = 4.
Total = 14 structures, but only **10 manholes** on the face of the type column. The four “Curb inlet” structures
(S-3, S-5, S-9, S-13) are already counted in 2.30 and are not labelled as containing a manhole; the memo has not shown
that a Type G curb inlet includes a 5-ft manhole. If the County confirms that every curb inlet also contains a manhole,
14 could be defended; on the issued plan the type column supports 10. The memo's own list of nine curb inlets includes
five structures that also contain a junction manhole (S-2, S-4, S-6, S-8, S-12); it then counts every one of the 14
structures again as a manhole.

**Correct 2.35 (base item only):** 10 × $8,750 = **$87,500**, not $122,500. Change from carried = −$2,100, not
+$32,900. With only this correction, Section 2 = $1,276,934 − $14,550 (2.30) − $2,100 (2.35) + $13,800 (2.03) =
**$1,274,084**, and the bond would be ceiling(($3,579,631.75 + $1,274,084 + $500,000)/1,000)×1,000 =
**$5,354,000**. The memo's $1,309,084 / $5,389,000 are therefore overstated by $35,000 / $35,000 relative to this
minimum correction.

**Evidence.** C-8 Structure Schedule, S-1 through S-14 (PDF pp.13–14): “S-1 5' dia. manhole (headwall/cleanout)”;
S-3, S-5, S-9, S-13 “Curb inlet”; S-7, S-10, S-11, S-14 “Junction manhole”; S-2, S-4, S-6, S-8, S-12 “Curb inlet +
junction manhole.” C-8 Design Note p.15: “All manholes are 5-foot inside diameter unless noted otherwise.”

### 2. MAJOR — The 60-inch manhole and catch-basin depth adders (2.38 and 2.31) are omitted; several structures are deeper than the schedule base depth.
**Requirement / basis.** Uniform Unit Cost Schedule items 2.31 (“Catch basin, Type A, depth > 6 ft, per additional ft”,
$475/VF) and 2.38 (“Storm drain manhole additional depth beyond schedule, per foot”, $685/VF). The C-8 schedule gives
rim and invert-out elevations, so depth is a plan dimension, not a missing dimension.

**What the deliverable has.** 2.35 is priced at the 60-inch base item for “depth ≤ 10 ft” with no 2.38 addition; 2.30 is
priced at the Type A base item for “depth ≤ 6 ft” with no 2.31 addition (Requirements register REQ022 and REQ025
expressly say “Not applied”; the instruction contains no such exemption).

**What it should be.** Using depth = rim − invert out from the C-8 table:
- Nine curb inlets, depth 7.77 to 15.31 ft; additional depth over 6 ft = 46.43 VF; 2.31 addition = 46.43 × $475 =
  **$22,054.25**. Correct 2.30 (9 EA) = $43,650 + $22,054.25 = **$65,704.25**.
- Ten manholes, depth 7.00 to 15.74 ft; additional depth over 10 ft = 22.02 VF; 2.38 addition = 22.02 × $685 =
  **$15,083.70**. Correct 2.35 (10 EA) = $87,500 + $15,083.70 = **$102,583.70**.
- With both depth additions (and the corrected 10 manholes), Section 2 = $1,276,934 − $58,200 + $65,704.25 −
  $89,600 + $102,583.70 + $13,800 = **$1,311,221.95**; bond = **$5,391,000**.
If the memo's 14-EA count is accepted, the 2.38 addition is still required for S-9 (2.77 VF) and S-13 (5.31 VF) plus the
22.02 VF above, or 30.10 VF × $685 = $20,618.50, making 2.35 $143,118.50 and Section 2 $1,329,702.50 (bond
$5,410,000). Either way the memo's $1,309,084 is below the schedule-required figure; it is not a conservative
estimate.

**Evidence.** C-8 schedule rim/invert values: e.g. S-6 rim 2,876.10 / invert out 2,865.39 = 10.71 ft; S-8 2,874.94 −
2,862.86 = 12.08 ft; S-14 2,872.10 − 2,856.36 = 15.74 ft; S-13 2,872.55 − 2,857.24 = 15.31 ft. Schedule items 2.31 and
2.38, p.3.

### 3. MAJOR — The catch-basin line was re-priced as Type A and reduced from 12 to 9, but C-8 requires Type G; the C-9 “Detail 1 Type A” cited in the memo is not in the issued C-9.
**Requirement / basis.** Instruction: “Flag an item only where the schedule has nothing matching what the plans show,
and leave the amount already carried in the subtotal for anything you flag.” C-8 Storm Drain Design Notes p.15:
“Curb inlets are Type G with 8-foot opening per Clark County Standard Drawing SD-305.”

**What the deliverable has.** Memo §3 and the cross-check note: “C-9 Detail 1 says Type A per CCUSD 411. The schedule
has no Type G item, so Type A item 2.30 is used for the nine C-8 curb inlets.” 2.30 is changed 12 → 9 EA, −$14,550.

**What it should be.** The issued C-9 (pp.16–18) contains the storage table, Sections A–A′/B–B′, spillway, outlet
structure and access-ramp details; it contains **no catch-basin Detail 1** and no Type A callout. The only plan
statement on catch-basin type is C-8's Type G. The schedule has no Type G item. On the documents actually issued, 2.30
therefore has no schedule match and must be flagged; the carried 12 × $4,850 = **$58,200** stays in the subtotal under
the instruction. The memo's −$14,550 is not authorised, and the internal QA/QC checklist's reference to “Detail 1/C-9”
does not make that detail part of the issued plan set. If the County confirms a Type A substitution in writing, the 9
EA price still needs the 2.31 depth addition (Finding 2); but the memo has not obtained that confirmation.

**Evidence.** C-8 p.15 (“Curb inlets are Type G…”); C-9 pp.16–18 (no catch-basin detail); memo Attachment A p.6
cross-check note; `DSR_Ph3_QAQC_Checklist.xlsx` row 24 (the only place “Detail 1/C-9” is asserted).

### 4. MAJOR (bond basis) — The memo presents $5,389,000 as the revised bond while dismissing the 11.04 escalation reserve on a false premise and admitting the Section 9 lump sums have no executed 11.05 agreement.
**Requirement / basis.** Addendum No. 1 item 11.05 requires lump sums to be **agreed** by the subdivider and the
Department; item 11.04 requires a 3.0%/year escalation reserve “where bond term exceeds 24 months.” Conditions of
Approval, Public Works condition 9, requires final acceptance after a **two-year maintenance period**, and the Phase 2
SIA (Art. 4.3) keeps security in force until acceptance and any warranty period expires.

**What the deliverable has.** Memo §7: “No escalation reserve under 11.04 is applied because the record does not
establish a bond term beyond 24 months”; the memo later says “The provided record contains no separate executed
agreement; confirm the County's written agreement before posting. The $5,389,000 bond assumes those lump sums stand.”

**What it should be.** The record does establish a two-year maintenance period after completion (Conditions of
Approval condition 9; Phase 2 SIA Art. 4.3 keeps security until acceptance and warranty expiry), so the bond term from
posting to release is construction time plus 24 months — i.e. it exceeds 24 months. If 11.04 applies, a 3% reserve on
the corrected construction subtotal (about $146,600 on $4.89M) is required for each year beyond 24 months; the memo's
figure would be understated. Separately, absent an executed 11.05 agreement the default 5% + 8% + 10% Section 11
allowances would produce a much larger bond than $5,389,000. The memo's own caveat means $5,389,000 is not a definite
bond figure; it is conditional on a document not in the record. This is outside Section 2 but is directly material to
the requested bond answer.

**Evidence.** Conditions of Approval p.3 condition 9 (“two-year maintenance period”); Addendum No. 1 pp.11; Phase 2 SIA
Art. 4.3 p.3; memo §7 and cross-check note p.6.

### 5. MINOR — The 2.44 detention-basin excavation quantity is not reconciled to the plan geometry; 10,000 CY is the 6.4 ac-ft storage figure, and the C-9 structural volume to top of berm is 8.02 ac-ft.
**Requirement / basis.** Instruction: where the plans give no dimension or stationing, the carried quantity stands.
C-6/C-9 do give basin dimensions and a contour-area storage table, so this is not a “no dimension” item.

**What the deliverable has.** 2.44 retained at 10,000 CY / $97,500, with the reason “C-6/C-9 give the 6.4 ac-ft
allocation and basin geometry but no excavation quantity or stationing; carried quantity stands.”

**What it should be.** C-9 Storage Summary tabulates areas from 29,450 sf at elevation 2,851.00 to 57,180 sf at top of
berm 2,859.20 and a structural volume of 8.02 ac-ft. 8.02 ac-ft × 43,560 / 27 = **12,939 CY**. Average-end-area over the
same 8.20 ft, (29,450 + 57,180)/2 × 8.20 / 27 = **13,155 CY**. The carried 10,000 CY is approximately 6.4 ac-ft ×
43,560 / 27 = 10,325 CY — the storage allocation, not the basin excavation. At $9.75/CY, correcting to 12,939 CY adds
**$28,655.25** (to 13,155 CY adds $30,761). If the top 1.29 ft of the basin is built berm fill rather than cut, the
6.4 ac-ft/10,325 CY figure could be the correct cut volume; but the memo does not say that, and it describes the
10,000 CY as excavation using the 6.4 ac-ft allocation. The plan does give the dimensions needed to measure it, so the
“no dimension/stationing” reason is not sufficient.

**Evidence.** C-9 Storage Summary table pp.16; C-6 basin callouts p.11 (top of berm 2,859.20, bottom 2,851.00, top area
≈1.31 ac); C-9 basin notes p.18 (8.02 ac-ft structural volume to top of berm). The 6.4 ac-ft is the allocation to the
100-year WSE, not the total excavation. The open CC-PW comment G-3 (basin volume reconciliation) is also omitted from
the memo's list of outstanding items, and the 09/25/2026 preliminary detention calculation (`DSR_Ph3_Detention_Calc_prelim.xlsx`)
reports a required volume of 8.1 ac-ft, not 6.4 — another reason the 10,000 CY / 6.4 ac-ft basis needs reconciliation.

### 6. MINOR — The basin access ramp was flagged as having no schedule match, but schedule item 3.05 (6-inch aggregate base) matches the ramp surface and the ramp quantity is measurable.
**Requirement / basis.** Instruction: “Flag an item only where the schedule has nothing matching what the plans show.” C-6/C-9: ramp 15 ft wide, 6% grade from top of berm 2,859.20 to basin bottom 2,851.00, surface 6-inch aggregate base course.

**What the deliverable has.** Memo §5, Table 4: access ramp “2,050 SF = 227.8 SY”; “2.47 is an access ramp but includes 4-in AC over 6-in aggregate base at $32.00/SY; the plan shows 6-in aggregate base only”; amount added $0. The memo says the closest analogue (2.47) would add about $7,300.

**What it should be.** Schedule item 3.05 is “Aggregate base course, Type II, 6-inch thickness” at **$9.25/SY**, which is exactly the ramp surface specified; the 2.47 item is not the closest match. 8.20 ft / 0.06 = 136.67 LF; 136.67 × 15 = 2,050 SF = 227.78 SY; 227.78 × $9.25 = **$2,106.94**. The ramp is a Section 2 detention-basin appurtenance, so this belongs in the Section 2 reconciliation even though the unit price sits in schedule Section 3. The memo's “no exact match” conclusion is wrong; at most it should explain why it declines to use 3.05.

**Evidence.** C-9 Access Ramp detail p.18; C-6 p.11 (“ramp surface to be 6-inch aggregate base course”); schedule item 3.05 p.3; memo Table 4 p.3.

### 7. MINOR — The memo misstates the C-9 spillway freeboard conflict and resolves it to the wrong value.
**Requirement / basis.** C-9 p.17 says weir crest 2,858.50 is “0.71′ above 100-year water surface”; C-9 p.18 says
“0.60′ above the 100-year water surface.” The tabulated 100-year WSE is 2,857.91, so 2,858.50 − 2,857.91 = **0.59 ft**.

**What the deliverable has.** Cross-check note p.6: “C-9 gives 0.71 ft in one callout and 0.60 ft in the basin notes;
the tabulated difference from 2,857.91 ft is 0.59 ft. No cost impact on the flagged ACB; correct the note at
resubmittal.”

**What it should be.** The memo correctly notices the inconsistency but does not state that both callouts are wrong;
it should say the governing value is 0.59 ft and require both callouts to be corrected. This does not change the
Section 2 cost but is an unresolved plan-note conflict that a reviewer should not leave as “0.71 or 0.60.”

**Evidence.** C-9 pp.17–18; C-6 p.11 WSE 2,857.91.

### 8. MINOR — The memo over-applies the “no dimension or stationing” instruction to items that are not shown on C-6/C-8/C-9 at all (notably 2.34 drop inlets and 2.46 fencing).
**Requirement / basis.** Instruction: “Where the plans give no dimension or stationing for a line item already in the
estimate, the quantity already carried stands.” That clause preserves a quantity for an item that is shown but not
dimensioned; it does not establish a plan basis for an item that is absent.

**What the deliverable has.** 2.34 “Drop inlet, area drain” 2 EA $7,800 and 2.46 “Detention basin fencing” 1,400 LF
$47,600 are retained with the reason “no dimension or stationing.”

**What it should be.** C-8 shows nine curb inlets and no area drains; C-6/C-9 show a vehicle gate but no perimeter
fence length. These lines should be flagged as “no plan basis — retained per instruction only if the County accepts
the carried allowance,” or a plan basis should be identified. This is a reconciliation completeness issue; the
instruction does not expressly direct removal, so the amounts need not be changed, but the memo should not present
“no dimension” as the reason without saying the items are not depicted.

**Evidence.** C-8 schedule pp.13–14 (types; no area drain); C-9 p.18 (gate only); memo Attachment A table 5 rows
2.34/2.46.

### 9. MINOR — Arithmetic and format checks that pass.
The DOCX opens, has 6 pages, and `ahpele_check.py` reports no problems. The filename, date (10/31/2026), addressee,
signature block and the three requested answers are present. Section 2 carried extensions sum to $1,276,934; the
memo's row arithmetic ($1,276,934 − $14,550 + $32,900 + $13,800 = $1,309,084) is correct for its stated assumptions;
Sections 1 and 3–8 sum to $3,579,631.75; the grand total $5,388,715.75 rounds to $5,389,000. The pipe takeoff from
C-8 stations is correct: 869.58 → 870 LF, 686.51 → 687 LF, and 1,333.56 → 1,334 LF (including 240 LF R14). The
30-inch outlet length is correctly 100 LF from (2,851.00 − 2,850.75)/0.0025. These findings are favourable and do not
offset Findings 1–4.

## Bottom line

The memo's $1,309,084 / $5,389,000 cannot be accepted as the corrected Section 2 result. The minimum clear error is
the 2.35 quantity (10 manholes, not 14): that alone gives **$1,274,084** and a **$5,354,000** bond. Adding the
schedule-required depth items gives **$1,311,221.95** / **$5,391,000** if the Type A substitution is accepted; if the
C-8 Type G requirement is honoured under the “flag, don't invent a price” rule, the 2.30 carried amount stays and the
result is **$1,303,717.70** / **$5,384,000**. The 2.44 basin excavation is a further potential **+$28,655**, and the
access ramp is a further **+$2,107**. The corrected subtotal must be recomputed after the Type G/Type A, 2.44 and ramp
questions are resolved; it is not $1,309,084. The $5,389,000 bond also assumes no 11.04 escalation reserve; the
two-year maintenance period in the Conditions makes that assumption doubtful, so the final bond figure is not settled.

PREFACE
The Uniform Unit Cost Schedule is published by Clark County Public Works for use by engineers of record, developers,
and sureties in preparing an engineer's estimate of probable cost for subdivision improvements offered for bonding under
Clark County Code Title 30 and the Uniform Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction Off-Site
Improvements (Clark County Area).
Unit prices set forth in this schedule reflect current Southern Nevada construction market conditions as surveyed by the
Department across the twelve-month period preceding the effective date, drawing on bid tabulations for publicly bid
subdivision and off-site improvement work in unincorporated Clark County and the incorporated municipalities of the Las
Vegas Valley. The schedule is intended to normalize bonding across projects and to remove unit price disputes from the
plan check cycle.
Engineer's estimates for subdivision performance and labor-and-material bonds submitted to Clark County shall use the
unit prices published in this schedule unless project-specific pricing is documented in writing (three qualified
subcontractor quotes or an executed prime contract, dated within ninety (90) days of estimate submittal) and approved by
Clark County Development Review prior to bond posting. Where project-specific pricing is approved, the higher of the
two unit prices shall govern for bonding purposes.
Contingency, mobilization, and design/inspection allowances stated in Section 11 shall be applied to the sum of itemized
construction cost in every engineer's estimate submitted for bonding.
ESCALATION AND REVIEW
This schedule is reviewed annually by the Department. Revised schedules are issued each January, with an effective date
of 01/01 of the calendar year. Between annual issues, the Department may issue a mid-year addendum where documented
market conditions materially depart (±10 percent or greater on any category) from the published unit price. Bonding
accepted against a superseded schedule remains in force at the amount posted; renewals, reissues, and increases occurring
after a schedule effective date shall use the current schedule.
Estimates submitted within thirty (30) days after a schedule effective date may, at the applicant's election, be computed
against the immediately superseded schedule.

]

def shade(cell, hexcolor):
    tcPr=cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd=OxmlElement('w:shd'); shd.set(qn('w:val'),'clear'); shd.set(qn('w:color'),'auto'); shd.set(qn('w:fill'),hexcolor)
    tcPr.append(shd)

def set_cell_margins(cell, top=25, start=55, bottom=25, end=55):
    tc=cell._tc; tcPr=tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    tcMar=tcPr.first_child_found_in('w:tcMar')
    if tcMar is None:
        tcMar=OxmlElement('w:tcMar'); tcPr.append(tcMar)
    for m,v in [('w:top',top),('w:start',start),('w:bottom',bottom),('w:end',end)]:

        if node is None:
            node=OxmlElement(m); tcMar.append(node)
        node.set(qn('w:w'),str(v)); node.set(qn('w:type'),'dxa')

def set_repeat_header(row):
    trPr=row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    tblHeader=OxmlElement('w:tblHeader'); tblHeader.set(qn('w:val'),'true'); trPr.append(tblHeader)

def borders(table, color='9CA6B4', sz='4'):
    tbl=table._tbl; tblPr=tbl.tblPr
    tblBorders=OxmlElement('w:tblBorders')
    for edge in ['top','left','bottom','right','insideH','insideV']:
        el=OxmlElement(f'w:{edge}')
        el.set(qn('w:val'),'single'); el.set(qn('w:sz'),sz); el.set(qn('w:space'),'0'); el.set(qn('w:color'),color)
        tblBorders.append(el)
    tblPr.append(tblBorders)

def add_table(headers, rows, widths=None, font_size=8, header_fill='D9E2F3', align_right=True, bold_last=False):
    t=doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers))
    t.alignment=WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    t.autofit=False
    borders(t)
    # fixed layout so the declared column widths are honoured by Word/LibreOffice
    tblPr=t._tbl.tblPr
    layout=OxmlElement('w:tblLayout'); layout.set(qn('w:type'),'fixed'); tblPr.append(layout)
    if widths:
        tblW=tblPr.first_child_found_in('w:tblW')
        if tblW is None:
            tblW=OxmlElement('w:tblW'); tblPr.append(tblW)
        tblW.set(qn('w:type'),'dxa'); tblW.set(qn('w:w'),str(int(sum(widths)*1440)))
    hdr=t.rows[0]
    set_repeat_header(hdr)
    for i,h in enumerate(headers):
        c=hdr.cells[i]; c.text=''
        p=c.paragraphs[0]; p.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
        r=p.add_run(h); r.bold=True; r.font.size=Pt(max(6.4,font_size-0.5)); r.font.name='Calibri'; r.font.color.rgb=NAVY
        shade(c,header_fill); set_cell_margins(c)
        c.vertical_alignment=WD_ALIGN_VERTICAL.CENTER
    for row in rows:
        cells=t.add_row().cells
        for i,val in enumerate(row):
            c=cells[i]; c.text=''
            p=c.paragraphs[0]
            p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(0)
            if align_right and i>0 and isinstance(val,str) and (val.startswith('$') or val.startswith('-') or val.replace(',','').replace('.','').isdigit()):
                p.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.RIGHT
            r=p.add_run(str(val)); r.font.size=Pt(font_size); r.font.name='Calibri'
            if bold_last and row is rows[-1]:
                r.bold=True
            set_cell_margins(c)
            c.vertical_alignment=WD_ALIGN_VERTICAL.CENTER
    if widths:
        for i,w in enumerate(widths):
            t.columns[i].width=Inches(w)
            for row in t.rows:
                row.cells[i].width=Inches(w)
    for row in t.rows:
        trPr=row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
        cant=OxmlElement('w:cantSplit'); cant.set(qn('w:val'),'true'); trPr.append(cant)
    return t

def p(text='', bold=False, italic=False, size=None, color=None, align=None, after=3, before=0):
    par=doc.add_paragraph()
    par.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(after); par.paragraph_format.space_before=Pt(before)
    if align: par.alignment=align
    r=par.add_run(text); r.bold=bold; r.italic=italic
    if size: r.font.size=Pt(size)
    if color: r.font.color.rgb=color
    return par

exit_code=0
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""AHPELE requirement scanner (stdlib only; runs inside the task container).

Finds requirement-like statements in the text corpus written by
ahpele_index.py (/tmp/ahpele/corpus) so that hard constraints are not missed:

  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py            # scan: writes /tmp/ahpele/req_candidates.md and .csv
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --check    # coverage: lists candidates not yet reviewed
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --register FILE.csv|.xlsx   # register rows: is each value in the document it cites?

A candidate counts as reviewed when its ID (e.g. R0042) appears in
/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv (adopted) or /tmp/ahpele/rejected.csv (rejected,
with a reason). A whole document can be rejected by putting its path in
rejected.csv. The scanner is a recall aid: it misses requirements that live in
tables, drawings or images, and it lists many statements that are not hard
requirements. It knows nothing about any particular task.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import html
import json
import os
import re
import sys

OUT = "/tmp/ahpele"
STRONG = re.compile(
    r"\b(shall|must|is required|are required|required to|mandatory|not permitted|prohibited|shall not|"
    r"must not|may not exceed|no later than|condition of|subject to|is to|are to|(is|are)? ?limited to|"
    r"not (be )?(less|more|greater|lower|higher) than|not exceed|at least|at most|no more than|no less than|"
    r"maximum of|minimum of|is not allowed|are not allowed|will not be accepted|not acceptable)\b", re.I)
LIMIT = re.compile(
    r"(\b(not (to )?exceed|exceed(s|ing)?|maximum|minimum|max\.?|min\.?|at least|at most|no more than|"
    r"no less than|not less than|not more than|not greater than|up to|limit(ed|s)?|cap(ped)?|allowable|"
    r"permissible|permitted|threshold|tolerance|deadline|before|prior to|within|until|expires?|valid)\b|"
    r"[≤≥<>]=?|±|\+/-)", re.I)
NUMBER = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z])[-+]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?")
NOISE = re.compile(r"^(--- page \d+ ---|page \d+( of \d+)?|\W*)$", re.I)
MAX_LEN = 320
TAG = re.compile(r"<[^<>]{1,400}>")
# folders that usually hold general reference material (codes, standards, catalogues) rather than project documents
REFERENCE = re.compile(r"(^|/)(library|libraries|reference|references|standards?|codes?|regulations?|catalogues?|"
                       r"catalogs?|vendor|manufacturer)(/|$)", re.I)
# file names of published codes and standards (general engineering knowledge, not task-specific)
STANDARD_NAME = re.compile(
    r"^(\d+[ _-]?CFR|UFC|UFGS|UFM|ASCE|SEI|ACI|AISC|AISI|SDI|SJI|IBC|IRC|IFC[ _-]?\d|IECC|IEC|IEEE|NFPA|NEC|NESC|ISO|EN|"
    r"BS|ASTM|ASHRAE|ASME|AWS|AWWA|API|ANSI|UL|CSA|DIN|AS|NZS|TIA|FM|NEMA|OSHA|EPA|FEMA|AASHTO|MUTCD|ICC|NCHRP|"
    r"USACE|EM[ _-]\d|ETL|DoD|IS)[ _-]?\d", re.I)
DATA_TYPES = {"csv", "json"}
VOID_DIR = re.compile(r"(^|/)(archive[sd]?|superseded|obsolete|old|void|withdrawn|cancell?ed)(/|$)", re.I)


def load_inventory():
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(OUT, "inventory.json"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            return {r["path"]: r for r in json.load(fh).get("files", [])}
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}


def statements(text):
    """Yield (page, statement) pairs: lines joined into sentences, table rows kept whole."""
    page, buf = 1, []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"--- page (\d+) ---", raw.strip())
        if m:
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            page = int(m.group(1))
            continue
        line = raw.strip()
        if NOISE.match(line):
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            continue
        if "\t" in raw or " | " in line or line.count("  ") > 2:  # table-like row
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            yield page, re.sub(r"\s+", " ", line)
            continue
        buf.append(line)
        if re.search(r"[.;:]$", line) or len(" ".join(buf)) > 600:
            yield page, " ".join(buf)
            buf = []
    if buf:
        yield page, " ".join(buf)


def split_sentences(s):
    parts = re.split(r"(?<=[.;])\s+(?=[A-Z(])", s)
    return [p.strip() for p in parts if p.strip()]


def scan():
    corpus = os.path.join(OUT, "corpus")
    inv = load_inventory()
    rows = []
    data_like = {d for d, r in inv.items() if r.get("type") in DATA_TYPES}
    for dp, _, fns in os.walk(corpus):
        for fn in sorted(fns):
            if not fn.endswith(".txt"):
                continue
            full = os.path.join(dp, fn)
            doc = os.path.relpath(full, corpus)[:-4]
            try:
                text = open(full, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
            except OSError:
                continue
            if text.count("<") > 20 and len(TAG.findall(text[:20000])) > 20:  # XML / HTML: keep the text only
                text = html.unescape(TAG.sub(lambda m: "\n" if re.match(r"</?(p|div|tr|li|h\d|head|br|section|para)\b",
                                                                     m.group(0), re.I) else " ", text))
            seen = set()
            for page, st in statements(text):
                for s in split_sentences(st):
                    strong, limit, nums = bool(STRONG.search(s)), bool(LIMIT.search(s)), NUMBER.findall(s)
                    if not (strong or (limit and nums)) or (doc in data_like and not strong):
                        continue
                    key = s.lower()[:200]
                    if key in seen or len(s) < 12:
                        continue
                    seen.add(key)
                    score = (4 if nums else 3) if strong else 2  # 4: modal + number, 3: modal, 2: limit + number
                    rows.append({"doc": doc, "page": page, "score": score,
                                 "text": s if len(s) <= MAX_LEN else s[:MAX_LEN] + "…",
                                 "numbers": " ".join(nums[:8])})
    for r in rows:
        r["ref"] = bool(REFERENCE.search(os.path.dirname(r["doc"]))
                        or STANDARD_NAME.search(os.path.basename(r["doc"])))
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (r["ref"], r["doc"], r["page"]))
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, 1):
        r["id"] = f"R{i:04d}"
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv"), "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=["id", "doc", "page", "score", "ref", "numbers", "text"])
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)
    by_doc = {}
    for r in rows:
        by_doc.setdefault(r["doc"], []).append(r)
    lines = ["# Requirement candidates", "",
             f"{len(rows)} requirement-like statements in {len(by_doc)} documents (score 4: shall/must/"
             "not-more-than wording with a number; 3: the same wording without a number; 2: a limit word with a "
             "number, often context rather than a requirement). Tables, drawings and scanned pages are only partly covered: "
             "read those yourself. Status flags come from the FILE NAME; confirm which documents govern. Project "
             "documents come first; published codes and standards and documents in reference folders are listed "
             "last: the clauses that apply are the ones the project documents invoke. --check asks you to review the "
             "score 3-4 statements of project documents; use the rest when you look a requirement up.", ""]
    shown_ref = False
    for doc, rs in by_doc.items():
        if rs[0]["ref"] and not shown_ref:
            lines += ["# Reference folders (codes, standards, catalogues)", ""]
            shown_ref = True
        flags = inv.get(doc, {}).get("flags", "")
        lines.append(f"## {doc}" + (f"  [name flags: {flags}]" if flags else "") + f"  ({len(rs)})")
        for r in rs:
            lines.append(f"- {r['id']} p{r['page']} s{r['score']}: {r['text']}")
        lines.append("")
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]
    kdocs = {}
    for r in key:
        kdocs[r["doc"]] = kdocs.get(r["doc"], 0) + 1
    top = sorted(kdocs.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:10]
    print(f"requirement scan: {len(rows)} candidates in {len(by_doc)} documents -> {OUT}/req_candidates.md; "
          f"{len(key)} strong candidates in project documents to review"
          + (" (" + ", ".join(f"{d}: {n}" for d, n in top) + ")" if top else ""))
    return rows


def must_review(r):
    """Requirement wording (shall, must, is to, not more than ...) in project documents."""
    return int(r["score"]) >= 3 and str(r["ref"]) not in ("True", "1")


def read_text(path):
    try:
        return open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    except OSError:
        return ""


def check(limit):
    path = os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        scan()
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(fh))
    adopted = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "requirements.csv"))
    rejected = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "rejected.csv"))
    if not adopted.strip():
        print(f"{OUT}/requirements.csv is missing or empty: build the requirements table first "
              "(one row per hard requirement, with the candidate IDs it comes from).")
    ids = set(re.findall(r"\bR\d{4}\b", adopted + "\n" + rejected))
    rejected_docs = {r["doc"] for r in rows if r["doc"] in rejected}
    inv = load_inventory()
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""AHPELE deliverable checker (runs inside the task container).

Re-opens each deliverable the way the recipient's software would and reports problems:
missing or empty files, unreadable archives, CSV/JSON/XLSX/DOCX/IFC that do not
parse, placeholder values (TBD, NaN, ...), Python that does not compile.
Standard library only; uses ifcopenshell when it is importable.

Generic by design: it knows file formats, never anything about a task. It does

SUNDIAL ENGINEERING & SURVEY

4720 South Rainbow Boulevard, Suite 210  ·  Las Vegas, Nevada 89103

(702) 555-0142  ·  NV COA #C-3874

MEMORANDUM

1.  Bottom line

Section 2 is reconciled to the Phase 3 drainage plans and the storm drain HGL schedule. The corrected Section 2 subtotal is $1,305,824.64, an increase of $28,890.64 from the $1,276,934.00 carried in the 10/10/2026 estimate. The revised performance bond is $5,386,000, up $29,000 from the $5,357,000 carried, after rounding the corrected total up to the next $1,000 under Uniform Unit Cost Schedule Section 12.02.

The correction has four priced components: the manhole count corrected from 14 to 10 and the plan-required 60-inch diameter in place of the 48-inch item (net −$2,100.00); the schedule’s additional-depth item 2.38 for the 22.02 vertical feet by which seven manholes exceed the 10-foot base depth (+$15,083.70); the missing 100 LF of 30-inch RCP from the basin outlet to the existing stub (+$13,800.00); and the basin access ramp, shown on C-6/C-9 at 2,050 SF of 6-inch aggregate base and omitted from the estimate, priced at schedule item 3.05 (+$2,106.94). The catch-basin line 2.30 is flagged: C-8 requires Type G inlets and the schedule has no Type G item, so the carried 12 EA / $58,200.00 stands under your rule. Five other plan features remain unpriced for want of a matching schedule item or a dimension; they are listed in Section 5.

Recommended action: release the corrected Section 2 subtotal of $1,305,824.64 and the revised bond of $5,386,000 to the surety broker, and reissue the estimate as Revision 1 with the Section 2 values below before it is transmitted. The Rev 0 estimate dated 10/10/2026 remains the sealed record until that reissue.

2.  Basis and documents relied on

The review is limited to Section 2 — Storm Drain and Detention. No other section quantity or unit price was changed. The following records were used:

Documents not used: the draft Detailed Team Review conditions (marked DRAFT, not adopted — the 03/14/2022 Conditions of Approval govern); the superseded 01/01/2025 unit cost schedule; and Phase 1/Phase 2 record drawings, which are prior-phase records and do not set Phase 3 quantities. No RFI or site instruction in the record changes the Section 2 scope.

Rules applied, as directed: (i) Section 2 only; (ii) published schedule prices, with an “Actual” schedule entry carried at the estimate amount; (iii) an item is flagged only where the schedule has nothing matching what the plans show, and the amount already carried is left in the subtotal; (iv) where the plans give no dimension or stationing for an item already in the estimate, the carried quantity stands; (v) pipe lengths are rounded up to the next whole foot. The final bond is the corrected construction subtotal plus the Section 9 lump sums, rounded up to the next $1,000 (Schedule Sections 11 and 12.02; Addendum No. 1 items 11.05–11.07).

3.  Section 2 reconciliation — quantity and unit-price changes

The table below is the complete list of changes. Quantities are from the C-8 Structure Schedule, the C-8 rim/invert elevations and the C-9 outlet and access-ramp details; unit prices are from the 01/01/2026 schedule. Extension = quantity × unit price, carried to the cent and reported to the dollar.

Change basis, item by item.

(2.35) C-8’s Structure Schedule types every structure: S-1 is a 5-ft manhole (headwall/cleanout); S-2, S-4, S-6, S-8 and S-12 are “Curb inlet + junction manhole”; S-7, S-10, S-11 and S-14 are “Junction manhole”; S-3, S-5, S-9 and S-13 are “Curb inlet” only. The manhole count is therefore 10 (5 manhole-only + 5 combined inlet/manhole), not 14. The four inlet-only structures are counted in 2.30 and contain no manhole. All manholes are 5-ft (60-in) inside diameter per the C-8 Design Notes, so schedule 2.36 at $8,750.00 replaces the 48-inch item at $6,400.00. 10 × $8,750.00 = $87,500.00 against 14 × $6,400.00 = $89,600.00, a net decrease of $2,100.00.

(2.38) Depth is rim minus invert-out from the C-8 schedule: S-6 10.71, S-7 11.29, S-8 12.08, S-10 13.49, S-11 14.03, S-12 14.68 and S-14 15.74 ft. The seven structures deeper than the 10-ft base total 22.02 VF of additional depth; 22.02 × $685.00 = $15,083.70. S-1 (7.00), S-2 (7.77) and S-4 (8.95) are within the base depth. Invert-out is used because it is the lower (deeper) invert and therefore the conservative reading; the schedule does not define the depth datum.

(2.03) C-9 shows the 30-inch RCP outlet from invert 2,851.00 at the headwall face to 2,850.75 at the existing stub at a 0.25% slope. Length = (2,851.00 − 2,850.75) / 0.0025 = 100 LF, already a whole foot. The pipe is outside the 2.45 outlet-structure lump sum (that item is the headwall, orifice plate and trash rack) and is missing from the estimate.

(3.05) C-6 and C-9 show the maintenance access ramp at 15 ft wide, descending from the top of berm 2,859.20 to basin bottom 2,851.00 at 6% grade, with a 6-inch aggregate base surface. Length = 8.20 / 0.06 = 136.667 LF; area = 136.667 × 15 = 2,050 SF = 227.7778 SY; 227.7778 × $9.25 = $2,106.94. Schedule 3.05 is exactly the specified 6-inch Type II aggregate base; item 2.47 is not used because it adds 4-inch AC that the plan does not show.

Arithmetic: $1,276,934.00 + (−$2,100.00 + $15,083.70 + $13,800.00 + $2,106.94) = $1,305,824.64. The net change is +$28,890.64. The full Section 2 line-by-line table is Attachment A.

4.  Pipe quantity check — no change

Pipe lengths were recomputed from the C-8 stations, which are the same stations carried in the HGL Pipe Schedule. Each diameter was summed by reach and rounded up to the next whole foot, as directed:

The 60-inch total includes R14, the Line B outfall reach from S-14 to S-15 (240 LF), consistent with C-8 and the HGL schedule. No pipe quantity or price change is required.

5.  Flagged items — no new price added

The catch-basin line 2.30 is flagged because the schedule has no item matching the Type G inlet the plans require; its carried amount stays in the subtotal. Five other plan features are shown on C-6/C-9 but have no matching schedule item or no dimension from which to quantity them; no price is invented for them. The existing items 2.42 (500 SY riprap), 2.45 (outlet structure, $28,000) and 2.46 (1,400 LF fence) remain in the subtotal unchanged.

The 2.30 flag does not change the $58,200.00 already carried, and the five unpriced features add $0, so these flags do not change the $1,305,824.64 subtotal. They should be closed before the bond is posted: for 2.30, obtain a Type G price or the County’s written acceptance of the carried allowance; for the others, either the County accepts the existing Section 2 items as covering them, or a project-specific or alternate price is approved under the schedule preface/12.04 and added in a future revision. If the County requires them priced, the bond will increase above $5,386,000. The closest published analogues would add about $4,300 for the grouted apron (2.43) and about $3,600 for the maintenance path if a 293-LF length is confirmed (3.05); the ACB spillway and the chain-link gate have no published analogue.

6.  Section 2 items reviewed and retained

The following carried items were checked against the plans and schedule and are unchanged. The reason for retention is stated for each.

The retained items above total $1,187,334.00; adding the corrected changed and added items ($87,500.00 + $15,083.70 + $13,800.00 + $2,106.94 = $118,490.64) gives the corrected Section 2 subtotal of $1,305,824.64.

7.  Revised bond computation

The estimate’s own sequence is followed: Section 2 is replaced, all other section subtotals are unchanged, the Section 9 lump sums are unchanged, and the final amount is rounded up to the next $1,000.

Section 9 note: the $350,000 mobilization/bonds/insurance and $150,000 contingency are the lump sums carried in the estimate as agreed under Addendum No. 1 item 11.05, replacing the 5%/10% defaults; item 11.02 design, survey and construction inspection is owner-carried under item 11.06, as stated in estimate row 189. The record contains no separately executed 11.05 agreement, so the County’s written confirmation is required before posting; if the lump sums are not confirmed, the default percentages apply and the bond changes. No escalation reserve under 11.04 is included: the Conditions of Approval (condition 9) require final acceptance after a two-year maintenance period, so the bond term from posting to release will exceed 24 months unless the County agrees otherwise, but the construction duration and the exact term beyond 24 months are not stated in the record, so the 3.0%/year reserve cannot be computed and is not in the $5,386,000. Confirm the term and any 11.04 reserve with Public Works before posting; if 11.04 applies, the bond will increase.

8.  Conclusion and recommended action

Section 2 is now checked against C-6, C-8, C-9 and the HGL schedule. The corrected Section 2 subtotal is $1,305,824.64; the revised rounded performance bond is $5,386,000. The difference from the carried bond is $29,000, reflecting the $28,890.64 Section 2 increase rounded to the next $1,000.

I recommend that Callaway: (1) direct reissue of the engineer’s estimate as Revision 1 with the corrected Section 2 values and the revised $5,386,000 bond; (2) transmit this memo and the revised estimate to the surety broker only after the Revision 1 estimate is sealed and the Section 9 and 11.04 confirmations are in hand; and (3) close the flagged catch-basin line and the five unpriced basin features with Clark County Public Works before bond posting, since a County requirement to price them would increase the bond above $5,386,000. Sundial will prepare the Revision 1 estimate and the flag-closure request; Callaway’s direction on the flags is needed before the 11/30/2026 resubmittal target.

The 12/18/2026 recordation target remains ahead of the 12/23/2026 successive final map presentation deadline under NRS 278.360 (the prior map was recorded 12/23/2024); the bond must be posted before recordation. This review does not re-verify Sections 1 and 3 through 8, landscape/turf quantities, utility capacity confirmations, fire access, the grading permit/SWPPP, or final map certificate conditions; those remain separate approvals.

Respectfully submitted,

_________________________________________

Max Braddock

Project Manager, Sundial Engineering & Survey

Dear Mr. Nokes:
Comprehensive Planning is in receipt of the written application submitted by Callaway Land Partners on
October 28, 2024, requesting an Extension of Time in which to present the first final map in the series under
TM-22-500041. This letter is the Department's response and, together with your application, constitutes the
official record for the tentative map file with respect to the extension question and the subsequent map clock.


--- page 3 ---
1. Governing statute — NRS 278.360
The extension mechanism available under Nevada law is set forth in NRS 278.360. In pertinent part, the statute
provides:
"The governing body may, upon written application filed after the applicable period has expired,
grant an extension of not more than two (2) years. An extension shall not be granted before the
applicable presentation period has expired."
The statute is written in mandatory terms and its two operative preconditions — a written application, and a filing
date after the applicable period has expired — are jurisdictional. The County has no discretion to relax them.
2. Disposition of the 10/28/2024 application
Because the Callaway Land Partners application of 10/28/2024 was filed before the applicable presentation
period had expired, the County is without authority to act on it on the merits. The application is not properly
before the County until the applicable period has expired, and the County therefore declines to act on the
request in advance of the presentation period. This is a jurisdictional disposition, not a rejection on the merits.
Nothing in this letter forecloses any future written application filed by Callaway Land Partners in compliance with
the statutory precondition, if and when the applicable period has expired and Callaway has cause to seek relief.
Any such future application would be evaluated on its own record and on the standards then applicable.
3. Presentation of the first final map in the series
The Department has been advised, and the Clark County Recorder's index confirms, that the first final map in
the series under TM-22-500041 — Desert Sage Ranch Phases 1 & 2 (100 residential lots on approximately 100
acres, together with a remainder parcel for future Phase 3) — has been presented and recorded of record. The
applicant may consult the Recorder's public index for the recording particulars.
The four-year first-map presentation clock that runs from the date of tentative map approval has accordingly
been satisfied and is no longer at issue with respect to Desert Sage Ranch.
4. Presentation clock for successive final maps
The applicable statutory framework under NRS 278.360 continues to govern the tentative map. The applicant
and its design consultants are directed to confirm the operative presentation deadline for any successive map
with Comprehensive Planning. Failure to timely present a successive map within the applicable statutory period
would terminate all further proceedings under TM-22-500041.
5. Notes for the file
• No fee refund is issued; the application fee submitted with the 10/28/2024 filing has been retained per the
Department's fee schedule for processing of the written record and this response.
• This letter has been indexed to the TM-22-500041 file and copied to Public Works Development Review
for coordination with any Phase 3 improvement plan and final map application that may be submitted in due
course.


--- page 4 ---
• Any technical, procedural or statutory questions on the successive-map clock should be directed to the
undersigned in writing so that the response may be added to the same file.
Please do not hesitate to contact me directly with any questions regarding the foregoing.

# Disposition of findings — revising engineer, 10/31/2026

The findings were re-checked against the instruction and the source documents before any change. The deliverables were
revised in place. Final figures: **Section 2 = $1,305,824.64** (carried $1,276,934.00; net **+$28,890.64**) and
**bond = $5,386,000** (carried $5,357,000; +$29,000). The numbered findings are disposed of as follows.

**Finding 1 — manhole count 10, not 14: ACCEPTED.** C-8 pp.13–14 types each structure: S-1 (5-ft manhole/headwall),
S-7, S-10, S-11 and S-14 (junction manhole) = 5; S-2, S-4, S-6, S-8 and S-12 (curb inlet + junction manhole) = 5;
total 10. S-3, S-5, S-9 and S-13 are curb-inlet-only and are counted in 2.30. 2.35 is now 10 EA at the 60-inch price
($87,500), a net **−$2,100** against the carried 14 × $6,400 ($89,600). The prior memo's statement that C-8 gives no
separate manhole count was wrong and has been removed.

**Finding 2 — depth adders: ACCEPTED IN PART.** Schedule item 2.38 is applied to the manholes: depth = rim − invert-out
from C-8, and seven manholes exceed the 10-ft base by 22.02 VF (S-6 0.71, S-7 1.29, S-8 2.08, S-10 3.49, S-11 4.03,
S-12 4.68, S-14 5.74), giving **+$15,083.70**. Item 2.31 (catch-basin depth) is **not** applied because 2.30 is a
flagged Type G allowance with no matching schedule base; attaching a Type A depth adder to a flagged non-matching line
would be inconsistent. The manhole depth adder is computed on invert-out (the lower, deeper invert), the conservative
reading, because the schedule does not define the datum.

**Finding 3 — Type G catch basin, 2.30 flagged: ACCEPTED.** C-8 p.15 requires Type G with an 8-ft opening per SD-305;
the schedule has only Type A (2.30) and Type B (2.32). The prior memo's "C-9 Detail 1 Type A" is not on the issued C-9
(pp.16–18) — that reference exists only in the internal QA/QC checklist. 2.30 is now flagged and the carried
12 EA / **$58,200** stays in the subtotal under the instruction's flag rule. The unauthorised −$14,550 is removed. The
plan count of 9 is stated in the memo and in the flag table.

**Finding 4 — 11.04 escalation and 11.05 lump sums: ACCEPTED IN PART (caveat), NOT AS A BOND CHANGE.** The reviewer is
right that the prior memo's premise ("the record does not establish a bond term beyond 24 months") was too strong:
Conditions of Approval condition 9 requires final acceptance after a two-year maintenance period, and Phase 2 SIA
Art. 4.3 keeps security until acceptance and warranty expiry. The memo now says the term will exceed 24 months unless
the County agrees otherwise and that 11.04's 3.0%/year reserve may apply. It does **not** change the bond number for
three reasons: (i) the construction duration and the exact term beyond 24 months are not in the record, so a
3.0%/year reserve cannot be computed without inventing a term; (ii) Section 9 is outside the instructed Section 2
scope and the estimate's own Section 9 basis is the $350,000/$150,000 lump sums; (iii) the record has no executed
11.05 agreement, so the memo states that written County confirmation is required and that the bond will change if the
lump sums or 11.04 treatment are not confirmed. The $5,386,000 is therefore stated as the estimate-based bond, with
the 11.04 exposure expressly reserved, not silently omitted.

**Finding 5 — 2.44 basin excavation: REJECTED as a cost change.** The C-9 storage table is a storage-volume table,
not a cut/excavation takeoff. Its 8.02 ac-ft "structural volume" to top of berm includes the 1.29 ft of freeboard above
the 100-yr WSE and the berm volume; the 6.4 ac-ft at the WSE is about 10,326 CY, and no existing-ground surface or
cut/fill split is given anywhere in C-6/C-8/C-9. The reviewer's 12,939 CY assumes the entire structural volume is cut,
which the documents do not establish. Under the instruction, "where the plans give no dimension or stationing for a
line item already in the estimate, the quantity already carried stands", so 10,000 CY is retained. The memo now states
the 6.4 ac-ft / 8.02 ac-ft basis and carries CC-PW comment G-3 as an open reconciliation item; it no longer presents
the 10,000 CY as a plan takeoff.

**Finding 6 — access ramp priced at 3.05: ACCEPTED.** C-9 p.18 gives 15 ft width and 6% grade from 2,859.20 to
2,851.00; C-6 p.11 requires a 6-inch aggregate base surface. Length = 8.20/0.06 = 136.667 LF; 136.667 × 15 =
2,050 SF = 227.7778 SY; 227.7778 × $9.25 = **$2,106.94**, added as line 3.05 in Section 2. Item 2.47 is not used because
it includes 4-inch AC that the plan does not show. The memo's earlier "no exact match" conclusion and its $7,300
analogue note are removed.

**Finding 7 — spillway freeboard: ACCEPTED.** 2,858.50 − 2,857.91 = **0.59 ft**. Both the C-9 p.17 "0.71 ft" and the
C-9 p.18 "0.60 ft" callouts are wrong; 0.59 ft is the governing value. The memo now says so and requires both callouts
to be corrected at resubmittal. No cost effect on the flagged ACB.

**Finding 8 — 2.34 and 2.46 reasons: ACCEPTED.** The amounts are unchanged, but the memo no longer offers "no
dimension" as if the items were depicted. It now states that 2.34 (drop inlet/area drain) and 2.46 (fencing) are not
scheduled or dimensioned on C-6/C-8/C-9 and are retained under the instruction, to be confirmed against the
C-4/C-5/C-7 grading sheets / wall-fence plan at resubmittal.

**Finding 9 — arithmetic and format: NOTED, RE-RUN ON THE REVISED FILES.** The reviewer's favourable checks on the pipe
takeoff (870/687/1,334 LF), the 100-LF 30-inch outlet, and the DOCX format still pass on the revised memo. The new
Section 2 subtotal and bond were recomputed from the submitted memo and the source records by
`/tmp/ahpele/check_section2.py`: every Section 2 extension, the delta, the construction subtotal, the grand total and

the ramp area are recomputed from the corpus. The requirements register re-runs at 55 rows, 0 not found / 0 unmatched /
0 multi; candidate coverage remains 590/590. `ahpele_check.py` reports no DOCX problems.

**Reviewer's bottom-line alternatives.** The reviewer's $1,274,084 / $5,354,000 (2.35 only), $1,311,221.95 / $5,391,000
(Type A substitution plus 2.31), and $1,303,717.70 / $5,384,000 (Type G flag without ramp) are superseded by the
disposition above. The final **$1,305,824.64 / $5,386,000** applies Finding 1 (10 manholes), Finding 2 for manholes
(2.38), Finding 3 (2.30 flagged, $58,200 retained), Finding 6 (ramp 3.05) and rejects Finding 5's speculative
12,939 CY; it does not adopt the Type A substitution because C-8 specifies Type G.

steps.message:
Final verification is clean: the deliverable exists at the exact required path, parses as a valid DOCX, contains every required answer, and all engineering/requirement checks pass.

## Deliverable

**`/filesystem/Correspondence/Client/Memo_to_Callaway_2026-10-31.docx`** — 7-page memorandum to Callaway Land Partners (Garrett Nokes) for Max Braddock's signature, dated **October 31, 2026**, with the bottom line, basis, change table, flag register, retained-items table, bond computation, conclusion/signature block, Attachment A (full Section 2 reconciliation), cross-check notes and action items.

## Final answers

| | Carried | Corrected | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **Section 2 — Storm Drain and Detention** | $1,276,934.00 | **$1,305,824.64** | **+$28,890.64** |
| Sections 1 and 3–8 (unchanged) | $3,579,631.75 | $3,579,631.75 | $0.00 |
| Construction subtotal | $4,856,565.75 | $4,885,456.39 | +$28,890.64 |
| Section 9 lump sums | $500,000.00 | $500,000.00 | $0.00 |
| Grand total | $5,356,565.75 | $5,385,456.39 | +$28,890.64 |
| **Rounded performance bond** | **$5,357,000** | **$5,386,000** | **+$29,000** |

## Priced changes

| Item | Change | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| 2.35 | Manholes **14 → 10 EA**; 48-in $6,400 → 60-in $8,750: **−$2,100.00** | C-8 pp.13–14; Schedule 2.36 |
| 2.38 | Manhole depth beyond 10 ft: **22.02 VF × $685 = +$15,083.70** | C-8 rim/invert-out; Schedule 2.38 |
| 2.03 | Missing 30-in RCP basin outlet: **100 LF × $138 = +$13,800.00** | C-9 pp.16–18; Schedule 2.03 |
| 3.05 | Missing basin access ramp: **227.7778 SY × $9.25 = +$2,106.94** | C-6 p.11 / C-9 p.18; Schedule 3.05 |

Manholes: 10 by C-8 type (S-1, S-2, S-4, S-6, S-7, S-8, S-10, S-11, S-12, S-14); the four inlet-only structures are in 2.30.

## Flags / retentions

- **2.30 Type G curb inlets — flagged; carried 12 EA / $58,200 retained.** C-8 requires Type G per SD-305; schedule has only Type A/B. Plan count 9 stated.
- **$0 flags:** emergency spillway ACB, grouted riprap apron, maintenance path, vehicle gate, topsoil/hydroseed — no matching schedule item or no dimension; no price invented.
- **Retained:** 2.04/2.06/2.08 pipe (870/687/1,334 LF), 2.34, 2.39, 2.40, 2.42, 2.44 (10,000 CY, no cut/fill takeoff; G-3 open), 2.45 (Actual $28,000), 2.46, 2.99 — **$1,187,334.00**.
- **Bond caveats:** 11.05 lump sums need written County confirmation; the two-year maintenance period likely makes the bond term exceed 24 months, so 11.04’s 3%/year reserve may apply but is not computable from the record and is not in the $5,386,000. Both are expressly reserved.

## Verification

- `ahpele_check.py` on the memo: **no problems**, valid DOCX, 7 pages, opens in LibreOffice.
- Completeness script: all required strings/answers present; 9 tables; Section 3 has 4 change rows; Attachment A has 16 line rows + subtotal.
- `check_section2.py`: C-8 types/counts/depths, HGL 870/687/1,334 LF, 100-LF outlet, 227.7778 SY ramp, all extensions, subtotal **$1,305,824.64**, delta **+$28,890.64**, bond **$5,386,000** — **all assertions pass**.
- `ahpele_reqscan.py --check`: **590/590** reviewed, 0 outstanding.
- `ahpele_reqscan.py --register requirements.csv`: **55 rows, 0 not found / 0 unmatched / 0 multi**.

Supporting records in `/tmp/ahpele/`: `checklist.md`, `asks.md`, `requirements.csv`, `rejected.csv`, `reconciliation.csv`, `check_section2.py`, `independent_review.py`, `independent_review.md` (findings dispositions appended), `final_check.log`.
